title: Data Services Data Analyst - AML & KYC Expert
description:
Introduction & Summary

We are seeking a Data Services Data Analyst with expertise in Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Know Your Customer (KYC) processes. The ideal candidate will leverage deep knowledge of KYC, AML, and Financial Security frameworks to develop data-centric solutions. This role requires strong analytical skills, excellent communication, and hands-on experience in managing data-related projects.

Main Responsibilities

  • Oversee the business analysis process from idea inception to execution.
  • Conduct analysis and mapping of data flows and identify issues.
  • Collaborate with Product Owners and SMEs to ensure requirements align with business goals.
  • Translate business needs into test conditions for product testing.
  • Support the design of data architecture and validation of solutions.
  • Facilitate delivery through effective change management and report creation.

Key Requirements

  • At least 4 years of relevant experience.
  • Proficiency in SQL querying.
  • Experience with conceptual modeling techniques.
  • Good understanding of data concepts such as big data and business intelligence.
  • Proficiency in MS Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
  • Understanding of Agile methodologies.
  • Deep knowledge of AML and KYC processes.
  • Strong stakeholder management and project management skills.
  • Good understanding of workflow processes.

Nice to Have

  • Familiarity with SAS Enterprise Guide.
  • Experience with reporting solutions like Power BI or Tableau.
  • Knowledge of banking activities and compliance is a plus.
  • Experience in creating and maintaining Agile roadmaps.

Other Details

This position offers a hybrid work model with an expectation of 50% onsite and 50% remote work. The role requires strong written and spoken communication skills in English, as well as good knowledge of Dutch and French. A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree or equivalent experience is required, along with relevant certifications.

title: Collision Parts Coordinator
description:
AL Decatur - 115020

We put our team members first. You’ll receive a great salary and benefits, and experience the support and opportunity you deserve. You’re empowered to make decisions. You control your future.

Job Description:

The Parts Coordinator’s primary responsibility and accountability is to provide an exceptional and successful customer experience while proactively managing the process of ordering, receiving, storing, dispatching and returning parts for each repair order. The Parts Coordinator plays a pivotal role in the success of the customer’s experience by verifying the accuracy and quality of parts received in a timely manner as per the production schedule and vehicle needs.

Key Job Responsibilities

  • Ensure consistent execution of WOW (Wow Operating Way) plan.

  • Communicate all customer requests and needs to appropriate team members.

  • Work with vendors to order and receive all parts as indicated on the repair orders confirming the quality, correctness and quantity of parts received, accurately identifying parts necessary to complete repairs in the shop.

  • Ensure timely parts distribution to the shop in accordance with the production schedule.

  • Enter all parts invoices into the recommended Management Information System (MIS).

  • Label and track all parts by the R.O.# and store them with the vehicle and/or scheduled repairs; Communicate all Parts Price Changes (also known as Parts Price Increases - PPI) to all required team members.

  • Order and receive supplemental Parts in the MIS, monitor performance of parts, materials and sublet vendors. Ensure daily reconciliation of the parts vendor invoice history report (e.g. 043 Report).

  • Ensure invoices and credit memos are posted and filed/scanned in a timely manner.

  • Ensure vendor invoices have the correct negotiated discount to maintain proper profit margins.

Education and/or Experience Required

  • High School Diploma or equivalent

  • 1-3+ years of experience working with automotive parts (auto body parts is a bonus)

  • Customer Service Oriented and strong organizational ability to manage pressure and conflicting demands and prioritize tasks takes initiative in problem solving situations

  • I-Car Registered (working towards Gold Class certification)

Required Skills/Abilities ​

  • Communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing

  • Strong attention to detail and a high degree of accuracy.

  • Effectively manage a fast-paced environment, demonstrating multi-tasking ability while working under pressure

  • Working knowledge of vehicle repairs practices

  • Management Information System: Summit, Repair Centre

  • Working Knowledge of: Mitchell, Audatex

  • Parts sourcing: Car-part, Progi, APU, LKQ B2B

  • Solid problem-solving abilities

  • Above average computer proficiency

  • Above average organizational skills

  • Ability to keep up and succeed in a fast-paced working environment

  • Ability to work well with others and achieve common goals

  • Other duties as assigned

Other Requirements

  • Frequently required to bend, crouch, reach, handle tools

  • Lift in excess of 50 lbs. of materials

Job Description:

Internship - Spring 2027 / Fall 2027 Packaging Solutions Co-op


Collaborate with Innovative 3Mers Around the World

Choosing where to start and grow your career has a major impact on your professional and personal life, so it’s equally important you know that the company that you choose to work at, and its leaders, will support and guide you. With a wide variety of people, global locations, technologies and products, 3M is a place where you can collaborate with other curious, creative 3Mers.


An internship is a temporary position within 3M. Packaging Solutions Co-ops typically work a full-time schedule throughout a 20-22 week assignment. This position is limited to working 899 hours per service credit year. 3M provides eligible interns with a housing and transportation stipend in accordance with current policy.


This position provides an opportunity to transition from other private, public, government or military experience to a 3M career.


Applications on this requisition are reviewed and filled on a rolling basis; it is in a candidate’s best interest to apply as soon as possible. Interested candidates should include a resume as part of their application.


The Impact You’ll Make in this Role

As a Packaging Solutions Co-op, you will have the opportunity to tap into your curiosity and collaborate with some of the most innovative people around the world. Here, you will make an impact by:

  • Developing and implementing creative and innovative package solutions that span across all three business groups in collaboration with cross-functional team members
  • Supporting the modification and improvement of existing package designs, methods and/or solutions
  • Performing and coordinating package testing according to established protocols
  • Working with suppliers of packaging materials and/or contract packaging vendors to obtain price/cost estimates, sample/material needs, and design requirements
  • Creating, maintaining, obtaining, and analyzing packaging data that enables improvements in the packaging implementation and optimization process

Your Skills and Expertise

To set you up for success in this role from day one, 3M requires (at a minimum) the following qualifications:


  • Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution
  • Completed at a minimum of sophomore year (4 semesters) by the start of the internship

Additional qualifications that could help you succeed even further in this role include:


  • Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree or higher in in Package Engineering, Packaging Science, or Supply Chain from an accredited institution
  • Completion of Package Materials and Package Design & Development curriculum
  • Current cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher on a 4.0 scale
  • Previous experience in the packaging industry

Work location:

title: Laboratory Protection Program Integrator
description:
Posting Title

Laboratory Protection Program Integrator

.

Location

CO - Golden

.

Position Type

Regular

.

Hours Per Week

40

.

Working at NLR

NLR is located at the foothills of the Rocky Mountains in Golden, Colorado is the nation's primary laboratory for energy systems research and development.

Join the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR), where world-class scientists, engineers, and experts are accelerating energy innovation through breakthrough research and systems integration. From our mission to our collaborative culture, NLR stands out in the research community for its commitment to an affordable and secure energy future. Spanning foundational science to applied systems engineering and analysis, we focus on solving complex challenges to deliver advanced, secure, reliable, and cost-effective energy solutions. Our work helps strengthen U.S. industries, support job creation, and promote national economic growth.

At NLR, you'll find a mission-driven environment supported by state-of-the-art facilities, multidisciplinary research teams, and strong collaborations with industry, academia, and other national laboratories. We offer robust professional development opportunities, and a competitive benefits package designed to support your career and well-being.

To set our new team members up for success, this position includes a six‑month probationary period. This is a collaborative time to ensure successful long‑term fit, providing dedicated support and training as you become acquainted with your role and our organization.

Job Description

NLR’s Laboratory Protection (LP) group provides a secure, safe, and resilient campus for staff and visitors. The Program Planning and Management team within LP is responsible for advancing NLR’s safeguards, security, and emergency management capabilities through a wide range of integrated functions. These include emergency management planning, oversight of physical protection strategies and security operations, security planning, and performance assurance activities. The team also leads the management of Incidents of Security Concern (IOSCs), security risk assessments, and insider threat mitigation. Additional responsibilities encompass continuous program and process improvement, contractor assurance, issues management, and compliance with applicable DOE Orders and federal requirements. This multidisciplinary approach supports NLR’s mission while ensuring the protection of people, property, and information.

LP’s Program Planning and Management team is seeking a motivated, experienced senior-level professional with expertise in security and emergency management to integrate requirements, training, field execution, performance assessment, corrective actions, readiness activities, and lessons learned into a consistent, repeatable cycle of continuous improvement.

Primary Responsibilities:

  • Integrate Laboratory Protection security and emergency management requirements, policies, training, field execution, performance assurance, corrective actions, and lessons learned into a repeatable continuous-improvement cycle.
  • Translate technical requirements and leadership expectations into executable plans, measurable outcomes, and practical tools that support consistent field performance.
  • Plan, conduct, and evaluate performance tests, drills, exercises, after-action reviews, supervisor assessments, and other assurance activities to identify performance gaps and improvement opportunities.
  • Develop corrective actions with clear problem statements, accountable owners, realistic timelines, validation methods, and closure criteria; coach action owners and verify effectiveness.
  • Analyze findings, performance results, training outcomes, corrective-action data, and stakeholder feedback to identify root causes, systemic risks, recurring issues, and emerging trends.
  • Reduce repeat findings by converting validated lessons learned and performance gaps into targeted training, procedures, job aids, field guides, quick-reference materials, and process improvements.
  • Partner with program and training owners to align curricula, refresher training, readiness activities, and performance expectations with validated operational needs and current program direction.
  • Develop and maintain dashboards, scorecards, and other performance measures that communicate readiness, corrective-action status, emerging risks, implementation progress, and sustained effectiveness.
  • Lead complex, cross-functional improvement initiatives by defining scope and deliverables, assigning responsibilities, establishing timelines and validation criteria, coordinating stakeholders, resolving barriers, and confirming measurable outcomes.
  • Serve as a senior problem solver for complex issues spanning Emergency Management, Protective Force, Central Monitoring Station, and other Laboratory Protection mission areas.
  • Facilitate collaboration among programs, directorates, leadership, and external partners to resolve readiness and performance gaps and implement integrated solutions.
  • Prepare and deliver clear guidance, field tools, reports, presentations, and leadership briefings addressing performance trends, systemic risks, corrective-action effectiveness, improvement outcomes, and recommended priorities.
  • Confirm that corrective actions and process improvements are implemented, adopted in daily operations, validated through performance activities, and sustained over time.

Qualifications:

  • Performance and Quality Assurance: Ability to apply performance-assurance principles, corrective-action practices, after-action review processes, exercise and drill evaluation methods, readiness assessments, and training alignment.
  • Critical Thinking and Problem-Solving: Ability to evaluate risks, requirements, data, and alternative solutions; identify root causes; exercise sound judgment; and develop practical, evidence-based solutions to complex operational issues.
  • Systems Thinking and Integration: Ability to connect requirements, policies, programs, training, field operations, performance evaluation, and corrective actions into an integrated improvement cycle.
  • Complex Information Interpretation: Ability to understand, interpret, and apply complex data, terminology, procedures, laws, regulations, and technical or programmatic requirements.
  • Data Analysis and Synthesis: Ability to analyze and synthesize findings, corrective actions, training results, performance measures, and stakeholder feedback to identify trends, recurring issues, systemic risks, and improvement opportunities.
  • Coaching and Guidance: Ability to guide action owners, program leads, and managers in defining problems, developing corrective actions, establishing measurable outcomes, validating effectiveness, and sustaining improvements.
  • Facilitation and Project Leadership: Ability to lead cross-functional initiatives from problem definition through implementation and validation, including establishing scope, deliverables, responsibilities, timelines, measures, and reporting expectations.
  • Stakeholder Engagement and Influence: Ability to build alignment, facilitate productive collaboration, reconcile differing perspectives, and influence outcomes across programs, directorates, leadership, and external partners without direct authority.
  • Communication and Field Enablement: Ability to translate complex requirements, findings, risks, and improvement priorities into clear, audience-focused guidance, reports, presentations, job aids, field guides, dashboards, and leadership briefings.
  • Change Management: Ability to plan, implement, validate, and sustain operational changes from initial concept through adoption in daily field operations.
  • Technology and Reporting Tools: Ability to use Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, SharePoint, Teams, Smartsheet, and data-visualization tools effectively. Ability to learn and use corrective-action, quality-assurance, learning-management, and incident or exercise-management systems.
  • Attention to Detail: Ability to produce accurate, clear, consistent, and professionally formatted work products that meet organizational standards.
  • Adaptability: Ability to learn new systems and subject matter quickly, manage competing priorities, and remain effective in a dynamic operational environment.

.

Basic Qualifications

Relevant Bachelor's Degree and 9 or more years of experience or equivalent relevant education/experience. Or, relevant Master's Degree and 7 or more years of experience or equivalent relevant education/experience. Or, relevant PhD and 4 or more years of experience or equivalent relevant education/experience. Or, relevant JD and 4 or more years of experience or equivalent relevant education/experience. Applies extensive technical expertise, and has full knowledge of other related disciplines. Contributes to the development of new concepts, techniques and standards. Considered internal subject matter expert. Extensive knowledge of laws, regulations, principles, procedures and practices related to specific field. Excellent leadership, project management and problem solving skills. Ability to use various computer software programs.

* Must meet educational requirements prior to employment start date.

Additional Required Qualifications

  • Clearance: Must be able to obtain and maintain a DOE Q Security Clearance.Eligibility requirements: To obtain a clearance, an individual must be at least 18 years of age; U.S. citizenship is required except in very limited circumstances. See DOE O 472.2A for additional information.
  • Bachelor’s degree in emergency management, security management, quality or process improvement, industrial or systems engineering, public safety, or a related field. Equivalent relevant education and experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.
  • Working knowledge of DOE physical security and emergency management requirements.
  • Demonstrated experience in performance assurance, security operations, emergency management, or risk management within a regulated environment. Experience in a national laboratory, DOE, or similarly regulated operating environment is strongly preferred.
  • Working knowledge of DOE security directives, compliance requirements, and emergency management protocols.
  • Demonstrated ability to interpret and apply complex data, terminology, procedures, laws, regulations, and program requirements related to Laboratory Protection, emergency management, security, and quality assurance.
  • Demonstrated experience preparing clear, professional, and audience-focused documents for leadership, program owners, employees, and external partners.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications, including Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, and SharePoint, for document development, collaboration, communication, and reporting.
  • Strong project coordination skills, including the ability to manage competing priorities, multiple deadlines, and cross-program improvement initiatives.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, collaboration, and facilitation skills, with the ability to engage cross-functional teams and leadership, build consensus, and influence outcomes across organizational boundaries and with external partners.
  • Demonstrated critical-thinking and problem-solving skills, including the ability to analyze complex issues, evaluate risks and alternatives, and develop practical solutions.
  • Strong collaborative communication and stakeholder-engagement skills, with demonstrated ability to facilitate cross-functional efforts and build alignment across organizational boundaries.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working in or directly supporting a DOE national laboratory.
  • Direct experience interpreting or implementing DOE physical security and emergency management directives, and related requirements.
  • Experience leading performance-assurance, corrective-action, readiness, or continuous-improvement initiatives across multiple programs.
  • Experience developing procedures, implementation plans, after-action reports, corrective-action plans, job aids, or leadership briefings.
  • Experience facilitating collaborative document development and reconciling feedback from multiple directorates, program owners, or external partners.

.

Job Application Submission Window

The anticipated closing window for application submission is up to 30 days and may be extended as needed.

Annual Salary Range (based on full-time 40 hours per week)

Job Profile: Professional IV / Annual Salary Range: $100,400 - $180,700

NLR takes into consideration a candidate’s education, training, and experience, expected quality and quantity of work, required travel (if any), external market and internal value, including seniority and merit systems, and internal pay alignment when determining the salary level for potential new employees. In compliance with the Colorado Equal Pay for Equal Work Act, a potential new employee’s salary history will not be used in compensation decisions.

Benefits Summary

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance; short*- and long-term disability insurance; pension benefits*; 403(b) Employee Savings Plan with employer match*; life and accidental death and dismemberment (AD&D) insurance; personal time off (PTO) and sick leave; paid holidays; and tuition reimbursement*. NLR employees may be eligible for, but are not guaranteed, performance-, merit-, and achievement- based awards that include a monetary component. Some positions may be eligible for relocation expense reimbursement. Limited-term positions are not eligible for long-term disability or tuition reimbursement.

* Based on eligibility rules

Badging Requirement

NLR is subject to Department of Energy (DOE) access restrictions. All employees must also be able to obtain and maintain a federal Personal Identity Verification (PIV) card as required by Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12), which includes a favorable background investigation.

Drug Free Workplace

NLR is committed to maintaining a drug-free workplace in accordance with the federal Drug-Free Workplace Act and complies with federal laws prohibiting the possession and use of illegal drugs. Under federal law, marijuana remains an illegal drug.

If you are offered employment at NLR, you must pass a pre-employment drug test prior to commencing employment. Unless prohibited by state or local law, the pre-employment drug test will include marijuana. If you test positive on the pre-employment drug test, your offer of employment may be withdrawn.

Submission Guidelines

Please note that in order to be considered an applicant for any position at NLR you must submit an application form for each position for which you believe you are qualified. Applications are not kept on file for future positions. Please include a cover letter and resume with each position application.

.

Equal Opportunity Employer

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard basis of age (40 and over), color, disability, gender identity, genetic information, marital status, domestic partner status, military or veteran status, national origin/ancestry, race, religion, creed, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding), sexual orientation, and any other applicable status protected by federal, state, or local laws.

title: Terminal Operator III
description:
Job Type:

Regular

Plains is an industry-leading transportation and midstream provider specializing in transportation, storage, processing and marketing solutions for crude oil. We own an extensive network of pipeline transportation, terminalling, storage and gathering assets in key oil producing basins and transportation corridors and at major market hubs in the United States and Canada. The company is headquartered in Houston, Texas.

We’re on the lookout for passionate self‑starters who thrive in fast‑moving, collaborative, and innovative environments.

The Pipeline / Terminal Operator III role operates and maintains pipeline facilities and / or terminals including tanks, pipeline pumping stations, LACTs, and gathering facilities to ensure the accurate and safe transportation and storage of petroleum products. Terminal Operators work within terminal facilities while Pipeline Operators normally work at facilities up and down pipeline and gathering systems. They will assist with petroleum product movements in and out of pipeline terminals and/or pump stations and are responsible for the storage of products and custody transfers activities with connecting carriers and customers. They will accurately assess the quantity and quality of crude oil and/or refined products and perform general facility maintenance in accordance with company mandates.


This is a field-based role with frequent work in open environments with extremes of heat and cold, often in proximity to high voltage and/or chemicals, which requires safety accommodations such as protective clothing and equipment. This role is subject to callouts for work associated with Plains field operations and/or emergency response.

Job Responsibilities:

  • Performance of all Pipeline / Terminal Operator I responsibilities and work tasks with minimal supervision.

  • Performs daily inspections and minor maintenance on tanks, valves, vehicles, and other equipment.

  • Calibrates and performs minor maintenance on safety, spill response and measurement equipment.

  • Ensures daily security and SPCC/EPA or similar regulatory inspections are performed.

  • Monitors and maintains station activity reporting and related documentation to include a variety of reports and records covering readings, over/short documentation, and oil movement orders.

  • Controls pipeline inlet and outlet product flows during normal operations and responds effectively to abnormal and emergency conditions.

  • Completes pipeline and facility checks, reporting abnormal conditions and troubleshooting as necessary.

  • Safely operates all facility rotating equipment and valves, LACT and metering systems, and hydrocarbon drain systems, reporting abnormal conditions and troubleshooting as necessary.

  • Performs basic troubleshooting and repairs on pumps, motors, injectors, valves, meters and other associated pipeline and terminal equipment.

  • Performs damage prevention activities (e.g., completes required documentation, completes 3rd party One Calls, conducts inspections and monitoring of 3rd party ground disturbance).

  • Maintains the integrity of the pipeline, controlling the excavation and backfilling of curried pipelines, selecting the appropriate pig for the pipeline and the work required, selecting the appropriate pipe coating, and responding to abnormal conditions (e.g., stuck pig, hydrates).

  • Creates and uses Energy Isolation Plans to prepare equipment and piping and ensures zero energy before releasing equipment to maintenance; accepts equipment and piping at maintenance completion.

  • Completes daily over / short reporting on assigned areas and identifies problems or signs of issues in bulk fuel; assists in product loss/gain investigations as needed.

  • Responsible for assisting in the training of new employees.

  • Responsible for identifying and preventing potential conflicts or operational problems, including reviewing operations schedules such as shift schedules, product movements, vessel movement, etc. to prevent conflicts.

  • Directs and / or supervises company hired contractors and assists in conducting contractor safety tail gate meetings.

  • Provides an active role within the Incident Command System during response planning, exercises, or incident response.

  • Conducts effective shift turnovers.

  • Responds to abnormal and emergency events.

  • Accountable to inform senior personnel of hazard identification and near misses.

  • Demonstrates safe work practices following Plains’ safety policies and procedures.

  • Assists with any other pipeline / terminal related duties as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, and Experience Required:

  • High school diploma or equivalent.

  • Minimum two (2) years of relevant work experience at the prior level.

  • Ability to speak, read, and write English and the ability to perform basic math.

  • Ability to read and interpret pipeline maps, technical drawings, and technical schematics.

  • Ability to work in a team-based work environment, with strong communication and interpersonal skills.

  • Must be able to use a variety of tools and equipment including compressors, pumps, mixers, hydrometers, centrifuges, sulfur machines, gauge lines, temperature and H2S monitors, line locators, SCBA, fire extinguishers and scrapers as required.

  • Must be skilled in product measurement including gauging, metering, meter proving and meter proving as a witness and product sampling procedures; this includes knowledge of line, tank, and automatic sampling systems.

  • Must have basic computer skills (e.g., Excel, Microsoft Office, Word, etc.) and be able to enter measurement and other operational data into computer-based systems.

  • Ability to maintain qualifications to conduct wharf operations to include operation of marine and truck rack vapor control systems; must be able to meet the requirements necessary to obtain a Transportation Workers Identification Credential (TWIC) card.

  • Must be knowledgeable on facility work authorization permits, Emergency Response Plans, SPCC plans, operations manuals and other plans and regulatory requirements that pertain to pipeline / terminal operations.

  • Must be familiar with PHMSA and OSHA regulations.

  • Must have an outstanding safety record.

  • Ability to successfully complete company Haz-Mat training, required DOT operator qualifications to perform pipeline mechanical operations, and mandatory safety training.

  • Ability to work in moderate to heavy physically demanding working conditions, including working outdoors in an open environment with extremes of heat and cold.

Qualifications:

  • Valid US drivers’ license with a clean abstract.

  • Cleared criminal history (background) and satisfactory reference checks.

  • Compliance with the Company’s drug and alcohol policy including pre-employment screening.

  • This position is not eligible for employment-based visa sponsorship. Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S. for the duration of their employment.

title: Geographic Information System Supervisor - City of Birmingham
description:
TARGET CLOSE DATE:

10/02/2026

Grade 27

TYPE:

JOB SUMMARY:

The City of Birmingham is seeking a well-qualified, motivated Geographic Information System (GIS) Supervisor to perform administrative and technical activities to ensure the design and functionality of Geographic Information System hardware and software resources within the context of programs and policy directives. The GIS Supervisor must have extensive knowledge of terminology, methods and practices used in GIS mapping and addressing systems as well as knowledge of the standards for GIS indexing systems according to legal standards, local, state and departmental specifications and guidelines. The GIS Supervisor exercises considerable discretion and independent judgement in their work. The GIS Supervisor also assists in the coordination of hardware, software, and data cabling activities, service vendor contracts, planning and organizing system development through subordinate staff. This position is a supervisory level job. The GIS Supervisor may coordinate with subordinate supervisors to plan employee schedules and timelines for completing various assignments. The work performed by a Geographic Information System Supervisor is primarily conducted in an office setting and includes few physical tasks.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS:

The City of Birmingham provides competitive pay and comprehensive benefits packages to include medical and dental insurance, employer-sponsored retirement plan (pension), generous paid holidays, sick and vacation leave, and more. The pay range for this job is listed below:

$63,502 - $98,508

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

The following are job-related qualifications that are required for employment consideration for this position:


Option A:

  • Work experience supervising or working in a lead capacity in a GIS or IT environment to include training and reviewing work of coworkers or staff.

  • Work experience creating and editing (e.g., creating/editing fields, setting dropdown options, programing with SQL or Oracle) in GIS databases (Esri, ArcGIS, MapInfo).

  • Work experience maintaining a GIS database to include spatial analysis (e.g., modeling problems geographically) and data extraction (e.g., creating scripts to efficiently isolate data).

  • Work experience with database reporting software (e.g. Crystal Reports, ArcGIS data reporting).

Option B:

  • Work experience supervising or working in a lead capacity in a GIS or IT environment to include training and reviewing work of coworkers or staff.

  • Associate degree in Geographic Information Systems or related IT field.

Option C:

  • Work experience supervising or working in a lead capacity in a GIS or IT environment to include training and reviewing work of coworkers or staff.

  • Geographic Information Systems Certificate or Certification from an accredited organization (e.g., Alabama Certified Mapper Designation, US Armed Forces, GISCI, GISP ).

Option D:

  • Work experience supervising or working in a lead capacity in a GIS or IT environment to include training and reviewing work of coworkers or staff.

  • GIS Specialist in the Merit System.

TYPICAL JOB DUTIES:

  • Maintains and creates department interest and efficiencies by attending meetings, tracking productivity, creating reports, representing department findings in court, maintaining equipment, suggesting or creating department policy changes, creating or editing procedures, and maintaining physical and digital files.

  • Enters or modifies basic records in a Geographic Information Systems (GIS) database and/or on a paper map (e.g., property owner changes, property splits or combinations, jurisdictional assets, voting districts) using techniques such as coordinate geometry and keyboard entry of tabular data.

  • Enters or modifies complex or impactful records in external databases or internal Geographic Information Systems (GIS) databases (e.g., right of ways, roads, annexations, deannexations, new subdivisions, new construction, reconstruction) using techniques such as coordinate geometry and keyboard entry of tabular data.

  • Researches, verifies accuracy and completeness of, and assigns records to staff of GIS related information in preparation of it being entered into GIS database.

  • Engages on cross-department/municipality projects by working with others to establish goals and deadlines for projects, performing duties within scope of the project, and communicating throughout projects (e.g., attending meetings, producing reports) to stay informed or communicate progress towards goals.

  • Supervises staff by assigning and distributing work, directing staff in their job duties, monitoring progress of work, providing feedback and/or training.

  • Conducts training to provide knowledge and understanding of work processes to ensure compliance with procedures and standards.

  • Participates in new GIS vendor software or equipment selection.

  • Provides service to internal and/or external customers.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

Job is primarily sedentary involving sitting for long periods of time, but may involve occasional walking or standing for brief periods. May involve occasional light lifting of items or objects weighing up to 25 lbs.

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

Work is conducted almost exclusively indoors in an office setting. Work involves use of standard office equipment, such as computer, phone, copier, etc.

title: Experienced GMP Data Reviewer
description:
Shift:

Monday through Friday, 8:00AM - 5:00PM

Are you ready to work making the world a safer, healthier place? Join our mission to continuously move science forward; to innovate and advance all aspects of our business to improve the health and safety of our communities and lives.

Description:

The Scientist is responsible for the thorough review and verification of analytical testing data generated in the QC laboratory. This role ensures all test results are accurate, complete, and compliant with GxP regulations, approved CMC dossiers and validated methods and SOPs. The incumbent serves as a critical checkpoint between data generation and batch release decisions, while also managing testing trackers and overseeing QC operational workflows.

Compensation: $114,000.00 - 125,000.00 per year

The salary for this position reflects a variety of factors. Compensation will be determined based on the candidate’s geographic location, relevant experience, education, skills, and alignment with internal equity. Market conditions, budgetary considerations, and organizational compensation guidelines may also influence the final offer

Responsibilities:

  • Perform first and/or second-level review of raw data, chromatograms, calculations, and test records generated from analytical testing activities
  • Verify that testing was conducted in accordance with approved methods, SOPs, and specifications
  • Identify discrepancies, anomalies, or data integrity issues and escalate appropriately
  • Conduct trend analysis on QC data (including assay controls and reference standards) to detect signals, drifts, or systemic issues
  • Support and own Out-of-Specification (OOS) and Out-of-Trend (OOT) investigations, Deviations and Change Controls through data review and root cause analysis (RCA)
  • Own and maintain QC testing trackers (sample status, review progress, batch release timelines) to ensure full visibility of testing activities
  • Track open actions, deviations, CAPAs, and change controls to ensure timely closure and escalate overdue items
  • Manage documentation workflows, ensuring data packages are complete, reviewed, and archived in a validated data repository system (Veeva) in a timely manner
  • Support capacity planning by tracking testing volumes, resource utilization, and turnaround times
  • Apply data integrity principles (ALCOA+) throughout all review activities
  • Support internal and external audits/inspections by providing reviewed data packages and responding to data-related queries
  • Maintain up-to-date knowledge of regulatory requirements (ICH Q2(R2), ICH Q10, FDA, EMA guidelines)
  • Collaborate with internal and external teams to support project goals and meet research timelines

Requirements:

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related scientific discipline
  • Minimum 3-5 years of experience in a GMP QC laboratory environment
  • Experience with method validation, risk assessments, CAPA tracking, and change control tracking
  • Excellent organizational, attention to detail, and communication skills.
  • Able to handle multiple projects concurrently, self-motivated, and results driven
  • Proficiency in Office 365, LIMS, and other software
  • Experience with mRNA, biologics, or small molecule analytical methods is a plus

Find Your Place at Pace - We need you - your curiosity, your talents, and your drive - to help us advance this important work.

description:
Director - Industry Advisor (FINS)
The Industry Advisor (FINS focus) will be instrumental in taking the organization to the next level of performance, helping to scale the organization and its capabilities. This individual will have a deep understanding and experience in the Financial Services & Insurance industries, partnering with GTM and Delivery to drive growth strategies around our key accounts. The Industry Advisor is responsible for driving cross-functional growth strategies and influencing both new logos and existing clients to show key performance indicators from their engagements with Coastal.
Role Responsibilities:
  • Strong industry understanding, structured problem solving, strategic clarity, executive presence (verbal and written), and solutions to drive deliver growth
  • Represent Coastal at key industry events, identifying new growth opportunities and building relationships with key industry stakeholders
  • Act as the Voice of FINS to prospects, clients, and partners
  • Represent Coastal at Money20/20, focusing on Financial Services Cloud (FSC) and AI-driven wealth management.
  • Responsible for supporting the scoping and estimating of programs and projects
  • Guide "True North" sessions for Banking or Insurance executives to modernize legacy core-banking integrations via MuleSoft.
  • Co-sell, grow, and manage strategic prospects
  • Develop competitive analyses designed to elevate Coastal’s brand against competitors
  • Educate and enable sales, pre-sales, and customer success teams specific to sub-verticals and influence Coastal’s POV
  • Partner cross-functionally on relevant content for events, marketing materials, and partnered GTM activities
  • Support market-ready solution direction & growth strategy execution
  • Engage with Salesforce RVPs and AEs to partner on new opportunities, drive new projects, and become a trusted partner.
  • Develop competitive GTM strategies for the Insurance Brokerage or Private Equity sub-verticals.
  • Proven ability to build, manage and foster a team-oriented environment.
  • Provide leadership, coaching, performance feedback and resources to associates
  • Be a clear and consistent communicator with the team and leadership
  • Work with your team to create estimates aligned with the customer requirements, expectations, and agreed upon deliverables.
  • Coach, mentor, and grow Market team members
  • Travel as needed to support the sales cycles to close business
Experience/Skills Required:
  • 8+ years of consulting experience in delivery leadership relative to iterative software development, ideally Salesforce, in the FINS industry
  • 5+ years of Sales experience
  • Proven Portfolio Growth – you will be responsible for growing our Coastal customers
  • Deep industry expertise with a point of view of sub-verticals
  • Commitment to building long-term relationships with customers and winning business through trusted relationships
  • Consultative mindset and a dedication to learning in a dynamic environment
  • Understanding of and relationships within the Salesforce portfolio, along with newly acquired solutions such as Mulesoft, Tableau, Slack, etc.
  • Excellent communicator who can easily understand business requirements and think on their feet
  • Consistent record of building and running robust teams
  • Self-starter with the ability to multitask in a fast-paced and high-pressure work environment
  • Strong customer orientation and results-driven leader
  • Demonstrated ability to analyze and interpret data for value-based discussions
  • Must have full-time permanent US work authorization
  • Note – Determination of Senior will be based upon the candidate's previous relevant experience and depth of skills, and will be determined through our skills interview process
Additional Preferred Experience/Skills:
  • Experience leading digital transformation and large-scale change management efforts
  • Strong understanding of AI
  • Ability to engage and motivate teams
  • Bachelor’s Degree preferred, or equivalent experience
Why Coastal, and what we offer:
  • Flexible working hours with an emphasis on a life-work balance (in that order!)
  • Remote flexible work; plus company office locations in Palm Coast, FL; Atlanta, GA; Tysons, VA & Lexington, KY; travel as required to client locations
  • Unlimited Paid Time Off (RTO), 401K with Company Match, and Medical, Vision, & Dental coverage
  • Competitive quarterly bonus opportunities
  • Continuing education and certification reimbursements, specifically within the Salesforce and Snowflake ecosystems; plus occasional in-house competitions with spot bonuses
  • A flexible and fun team culture! We value transparency, support, flexibility, growth, teamwork, fun, and so much more
  • Frequent team and culture activities, virtual & in-person, including Lunch and Learns, Happy Hours, team-building events
  • Monthly All-Hands calls to bring the company together, and an open-door leadership policy with access to mentorship and guidance
  • Opportunities for accelerated growth, networking, and career guidance and support
  • Trust, transparency and respect across all levels of the company

title: Midas - Automotive Store Managers
description:
Automotive Store Managers

Join the World's Largest Midas Franchisee - Now Proudly Part of the Mavis Tire Family!


Put your career into high gear with Auto Systems Centers, the world's largest Midas franchisee! We have joined the Mavis Tire family, combining our rich history in the automotive industry with the support and stability of Mavis's national platform. We are currently seeking full-time Store Managers for our state-of-the-art service, repair, and tire center in Roswell, GA.


WHY YOU'LL LOVE WORKING WITH US

We offer a competitive package that respects your skills and rewards your dedication:

  • Competitive Weekly Pay: Guaranteed base pay plus significant weekly bonus potential.
  • Work-Life Balance: 5-day work week with Sundays and one other weekday off.
  • Invested in Your Future: 401(k) retirement savings plan with an employer match.
  • Comprehensive Benefits: Health, dental, vision, and life insurance coverage.
  • Paid Time Off: Paid vacations, paid holidays, and general PTO.
  • Career Growth: A commitment to promoting from within.
  • Uniform Support: We cover uniform expenses.

ABOUT THE POSITION OF STORE MANAGER

Automotive Store Managers are responsible for the management of a retail store location and ensuring maximum profitability by driving sales, monitoring inventory and expenses, managing personnel and controlling operating costs. In addition to implementing and managing sales programs, our Store Managers direct the work of technicians and mechanics to ensure the timely and safe completion of high-quality vehicle repair and maintenance. To advance Midas's sales initiatives, Store Managers communicate directly with customers, assess customer needs, provide information regarding requested and/or necessary automotive repairs and maintenance and ensure complete customer satisfaction. With our revolutionary digital dashboard, Store Managers can track their personal success and watch their weekly earnings grow as grow they lead by example to reinforce Midas's position as the premiere tire and auto service retailer.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

  • Experience: At least 3 years of experience in retail store management, or a relevant combination of education, training and experience.
  • Requirements: Must be at least 18 years old and authorized to work in the U.S.
  • Physical Ability: Ability to stand, walk, bend, and lift/move items weighing over 50 pounds.
  • Mindset: You value dependability, teamwork, and providing quality service in a fast-paced environment.

HOW TO APPLY

Apply now to join a team that values your experience!

  • Online: Visit https://midas.applicantpro.com/jobs/
  • In-Person: Walk into any of our stores for an immediate interview.

title: Technical Electronic Intelligence (TechELINT) Analyst
description:
Job Overview: Seeking Technical Electronic Intelligence (TechELINT) Analyst. Become a member of a highly accomplished ELINT team providing direct support to geographically dispersed USAF Wing and Squadron-level organizations. Perform interpretive pulse-level and P-Cubed analysis of ELINT data, in-depth radar and weapons systems studies, and cutting-edge modeling and simulation efforts.

The TechELINT analyst will leverage their aviation, Electronic Warfare experience, and critical-thinking prowess to develop tactics and techniques to counter emerging threats. The analyst will also work and coordinate with DoD entities and agencies to facilitate cutting-edge product development to ensure client capabilities meet current and future objectives. The analyst must possess an in-depth understanding of the key factors in aircraft survivability and combat mission planning to ensure client objectives are met.


Primary Responsibilities:

  • Support the collection, documentation, and post-test analysis of ELINT to evaluate programming effectiveness.
  • Use specialized tools to ingest intel data and program ELINT, ensuring integration with EW systems.
  • Work with a team of engineers to collaborate on ELINT products and ensure proper programming in alignment with mission objectives.
  • Design procedures to analyze testing results, ensuring accurate validation and effectiveness of systems.
  • Utilize the latest intel databases to perform detailed analysis and research, identifying potential threats and solutions.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree (or 2-4 additional years of experience) in Intelligence or Information Operations and minimum of 8 years ofTechnical Signals Analysis experience.
  • Experience with intel tools such as ASPEN, WILLOW, MARTES, THRESHER, and GALE.
  • Former Military Experience in Technical Signals Analysis.
  • Active TOP SECRET clearance.
  • Strong understanding of RF Signals fundamentals and technical solutions.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Familiarity with Air Force organizational structure, operations, and procedures.
  • Experience briefing Senior Management and Leadership.
  • Aviation experience with Strategic assets (RC-135, etc.)
  • Expertise in the latest electronic threats, indicators, and technical solutions.
  • Experience with tools such as MATLAB.

title: AI Engineering Lead
description:
Job Title: Sr. Software Engineer, AI
Location: Weston, FL
WFH Status: Preferred Weston // Fully remote is also fine
Duration: 6 months
Pay Rate: $65/hr - $70/hr (DOE)

Job Description:
The Planet Group is seeking a Sr. AI Software Engineer, this engineer is the delivery and mentorship multiplier of the AI engineering team, the senior builder who turns architecture into shipped solutions and models engineering craft for early-career teammates. The role is platform-agnostic by design: what matters is deep, current fluency in building production AI systems, agentic workflows, LLM integrations, retrieval patterns, evaluation: on whatever stack the problem calls for. Today's estate is Microsoft-centered (Azure AI, Copilot Studio, Power Platform), but we hire for the engineering, not the vendor. This person carries the team's most complex builds while raising the bar for everyone around them.

Responsibilities:

  • Design and develop agentic AI workflows -- multi-step, multi-tool systems with memory, planning, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints -- using the frameworks and model providers best suited to each use case
  • Build and maintain AI-powered solutions for finance and accounting use cases, spanning code-first services and low/no-code platforms as appropriate
  • Develop Python-based automation and AI integration code -- well-structured, tested, production-ready
  • Engineer prompt templates, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) patterns, and evaluation frameworks for enterprise use cases
  • Connect AI pipelines to ERP and enterprise data -- REST/OData APIs, data entities, SQL
  • Pair with and mentor the team's junior engineers; review their designs and code
  • Contribute to AI architecture decisions and architecture decision records alongside the AI Engineering Lead
  • Support organization-wide AI adoption -- demos, office hours, and internal upskilling content

Qualifications:
  • 5+ years of software engineering experience with 2+ years in AI engineering or enterprise AI solution delivery
  • Hands-on experience building against modern LLM APIs (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, Google) -- completions, embeddings, tool/function calling, structured outputs
  • Experience building agentic systems -- tool use, memory management, orchestration -- with one or more frameworks (e.g., LangChain, LlamaIndex, Semantic Kernel, Microsoft Agent Framework, or equivalent in-house patterns)
  • Proficiency in Python -- async patterns, API clients, data processing, testing
  • Experience with RAG architectures -- vector stores, embedding pipelines, retrieval strategies
  • Strong ability to write clean, maintainable, production-grade code with test coverage
  • Effective mentor and collaborator in a distributed team

Preferred Qualifications:
  • Experience with the Microsoft AI stack -- Azure AI Foundry, Azure OpenAI, Copilot Studio, Power Platform
  • Familiarity with enterprise ERP data structures and API patterns (Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations, SAP, Oracle, or similar)
  • Experience with AI evaluation and observability tooling -- eval harnesses, tracing, model comparison
  • Relevant cloud or AI certifications (any major provider)
  • Background in finance, accounting, or ERP process automation

title: Senior Associate, Contract Revenue
description:
At The Obama Foundation, our mission is to inspire, empower, and connect people to change their world. We seek to build an active democratic culture where people are equipped and motivated to make change in the communities where they live, work, and play. Right here on the South Side of Chicago, we’re building a home for this vision, a global center for change with a range of opportunities - coordinated programming, community outreach events, educational moments, and more - that invite visitors from down the block or across the globe to turn hope into action.

Achieving our ambitious goals starts with an exceptional team built on our Hope to Action Values - Courage, Empathy, Integrity, Accountability, Community, Inclusivity, Pragmatism, Resilience, Imagination, and Hope. A Framework that anyone, anywhere, can use to build trust, activate participation, and expand opportunity in their community.

Purpose of the Role

As the Senior Associate of Contract Revenue, Obama Presidential Center (OPC), you will report directly to the Senior Manager of Contract Revenue and support the Earned Income team by assisting with the development and execution of operational and administrative processes. In this role, you will work closely with the Center’s Food & Beverage Operator and Retail Operator, including collaboration during their onboarding, while also supporting management of the OPC parking facility. Your primary focus is ensuring contract compliance, revenue generation, cross-workstream coordination, and the highest level of visitor satisfaction, while prioritizing strategic objectives in alignment with the Foundation’s goals.

Core Job Responsibilities

  • Operational Planning: Support engagement with the Food & Beverage Operator and Retail Operator by streamlining internal processes through this pillar of revenue generation and experiential implementation. Work across Foundation teams to support the facilitation of marketing plans across revenue streams and operational plans to manage processes.
  • Compliance & Brand Standards: Manage review of Retail Operator contract compliance, addressing contractual obligations, customer experience, and alignment with Foundation brand and goals. Support in monitoring vendor compliance as it relates to diversity, inclusivity, and diverse sales strategies to further OPC economic impact.
  • Project Management: Oversee team project management by creating and maintaining project plans in Asana, tracking deadlines, following up with teammates on progress, integrating processes, and coordinating schedules for vendor and partner meetings.
  • Asset Management & Communications: Maintain up-to-date Earned Income-related assets (including slide decks and external-facing materials) as the primary point person. Ensure Operators comply with Foundation brand guidelines and experiential implementation.
  • Data & Analytics: Serve as an accountability partner to ensure existing and new processes work efficiently across the team, supporting the creation of a reporting model across revenue operations to provide performance updates.
  • Administrative Support: Organize and maintain shared Drive access, draft meeting agendas, provide recaps with next steps post-meeting, and ensure the Earned Income team has complete administrative support to execute strategic goals.
  • Parking Facility Support: Provide support to the Building Operations team in managing the OPC Parking facility. In conjunction with the Parking Vendor, establish a working understanding of revenue trends and parking price strategies to maximize revenue potential during peak periods while maintaining competitive, equitable rates during off-peak periods and showing sensitivity to guest needs.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Key Deliverables / Outcomes

  • Operational coordination and daily briefings across scheduled events and upcoming commitments.
  • Timely deliverables and content reviewed by all relevant leads from the OPC team.
  • Monitored and up-to-date Asana project plans, deadlines, and vendor meeting agendas/recaps.
  • Established reporting models and operational plans across revenue streams.
  • Optimized parking revenue strategy during peak and off-peak periods.

Required Qualifications

  • Experience in a customer service environment with a commitment to guest experience standards. Operational experience in a non-profit or customer-facing organization, with an emphasis on addressing diverse audiences through revenue and engagement strategies.
  • Experience designing and implementing effective, efficient systems and processes to manage complex projects, meet deadlines, and deliver results in a fast-paced environment.
  • Highly organized, with strong decision-making skills and discretion when managing short- and long-term responsibilities in a deadline-driven, high-volume environment. Demonstrates initiative and anticipates needs.
  • Graphic design skills and experience, including Adobe Suite, complemented by strong editing and proofreading skills.
  • Ability to work out of the Obama Presidential Center in Jackson Park and/or other Obama Foundation locations in Chicago. Requires schedule flexibility, including early mornings, late nights, weekends, and holidays, across indoor and outdoor campus environments.

The salary range for this role is between $79,040 and $98,800.


This is an onsite role based at the Obama Presidential Center in Jackson Park.

title: Network Engineer
description:
Network Engineer

Location: Naples, Italy

Security Clearance: Active TS/SCI Required

Leidos is seeking a Network Engineer to support forward deployed mission operations at the Office of Naval Intelligence (ONI) in Naples, Italy In this role, you will design, optimize, secure, and sustain large scale enterprise networks supporting critical Department of Defense communications. The ideal candidate has extensive experience with complex routing and switching, DoD communication systems, and enterprise network engineering in mission critical environments.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Oversee Local Area Network (LAN), Wide Area Network (WAN), firewall, and Network Management System (NMS) activities in accordance with Government guidance.

  • Manage advanced Cisco routing and switching for enterprise networks consisting of more than 700 Cisco routers and switches.

  • Configure cryptographic devices and advanced routing protocols, including Open Shortest Path First (OSPF).

  • Review Information Assurance Vulnerability Alerts (IAVAs) and Information Assurance Vulnerability Bulletins (IAVBs), and implement required remediation.

  • Support local network infrastructure and telecommunications circuits ranging from T1 through OC 192.

  • Develop Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and recommend improvements to the Government that enhance the security environment.

  • Provide onsite engineering support for operational mission environments.

  • Provide technical assistance to remote Hopper Global Communications Center (HGCC) divisions. Travel may be required to Guam, Japan, Bahrain, Italy, Spain, Australia, South Korea, and Singapore.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, an engineering discipline, or a technical discipline with 4+ years of experience, or a Master's degree with 2+ years of experience. Additional relevant experience may be substituted for a degree.

  • Active TS/SCI security clearance (in DISS).

  • Active CompTIA Security+ certification.

  • Active Cisco Certified Network Professional (CCNP) certification.

  • Engineering experience supporting DoD communication systems and networks.

  • Expertise in the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model, specifically Layers 1 through 4. Knowledge of systems and applications operating at the higher OSI layers is essential to the continued success of HGCC N31 and its supported customers.

  • Expertise with Cisco enterprise networking, cryptographic devices, and large scale routing optimization.

title: People Services Advisor
description:
Role: People Services Advisor

Location: Hybrid, based from our offices in Warrington


About Us

Rolls‑Royce SMR is here to transform how nuclear energy is delivered—cleaner, faster and at global scale. Our teams are developing one of the world’s most advanced small modular reactors, helping secure affordable, low‑carbon energy for generations to come.


We’re doing something that’s never been done before. We’re revolutionising an industry. That’s a once-in-a-career opportunity for those excited by such a challenge. This is more than just a job; this is a legacy.


The People Services Advisor is responsible for delivering expertise and guidance across the employee lifecycle, ensuring the delivery of efficient, compliant, and employee-focused HR, payroll, benefits, and HR systems processes. The role acts as a key advisor to managers and employees, driving continuous improvement, process standardisation, and operational excellence. Ensuring all activities are completed in accordance with company policies, employment legislation, service level agreements, and data protection requirements.

Success in the role will be demonstrated through the effective delivery of People Services support and advice, ensuring employees and managers receive accurate, timely and customer-focused guidance across the employee lifecycle. Maintaining high-quality people data, resolving queries efficiently with professionalism and empathy, and contributing to a positive employee experience while ensuring compliance with employment policies, regulatory requirements and governance standards. The role will also play an active part in identifying opportunities for continuous improvement, enhancing service delivery, and supporting the evolution of People Services processes and practices.


What we’re looking for


HR Administration & Employee Lifecycle Management

Experience in managing end-to-end employee lifecycle processes and offboarding activities. Ability to prepare accurate HR documentation and maintain employee records within HR systems to a high standard of accuracy and confidentiality.


Payroll & Benefits Administration

Experience administering payroll-related activities and employee benefit programmes, such as pensions, insurances, flexible benefits, and salary sacrifice schemes. Proven ability to reconcile data, carry out validation checks and resolve data discrepancies. Experience of working effectively with third-party providers to resolve issues.


Customer Service & Stakeholder Support

Strong customer service and communication skills with the ability to act as first point of contact providing expert guidance and advice to managers, employees, and stakeholders on People Services processes. Respond accurately and timely to queries and delivering a professional and positive employee experience. Build effective relationships with People Leaders, HR colleagues, Finance, Payroll, external providers, and other business stakeholders to support operational and strategic objectives


Experience using HR systems and Microsoft Office applications.


Location & Ways of Working

This role can be based in Warrington, with flexibility to work between home and the office depending on business needs.


What’s in It for You

title: Senior Software Developer — Scrum Master
description:
Leidos is seeking a Senior Software Developer — Scrum Master to join the Air Traffic Business Area within the Homeland Sector, supporting the development of the Leidos Common Automation Platform (L-CAP). L-CAP is a mission-critical, future-ready automation platform built on a hybrid cloud data mesh architecture, enabling next-generation air traffic management capabilities. This role operates within a SAFe/Agile framework as part of an Agile Release Train (ART) delivering iterative value across the program.


Approximately 50% of your time will be spent designing, developing, testing, and maintaining production software for the L-CAP platform, while the remaining 50% will be dedicated to serving as Scrum Master for an Agile development team on the ART. We are looking for experienced software engineers who enjoy facilitating Agile teams while remaining actively involved in coding, technical design, reviews, and software delivery.


This is a hybrid position requiring 3 days onsite and 2 days working from home, if you are located within a commutable distance (Less than 1 hour's drive one-way during normal traffic) from Gaithersburg, MD; Eagan, MN; or Egg Harbor Township, NJ. However, if you do not reside within a commutable distance, you may be considered for a 100% remote role.


This role focuses on building and modernizing real-time, safety-critical systems using a combination of traditional systems engineering and AI-augmented software development practices. You’ll work on software that directly supports national air traffic operations, applying AI tools to accelerate development, improve quality, and enhance system reliability.



Primary Responsibilities

  • Approximately 50% hands-on software engineering: design, develop, test, review, debug, deploy, and maintain production-quality cloud-native microservices while contributing to software architecture and technical design decisions
  • Approximately 50% Scrum Master responsibilities: facilitate Agile ceremonies, remove impediments, promote continuous improvement, and help the team deliver predictable sprint and PI outcomes
  • Guide the team through SAFe cadence including PI planning, iteration planning, backlog refinement, system demos, and inspect-and-adapt workshops
  • Track and communicate team flow metrics, velocity, and PI objective progress, using data to drive continuous improvement
  • Coordinate with the Release Train Engineer, Product Owner, management, and cross-functional stakeholders to communicate team status, risks, dependencies, and delivery progress
  • Manage cross-team and cross-ART dependencies, escalating and resolving blockers that threaten committed outcomes
  • Leverage modern DevSecOps practices, CI/CD pipelines, AI-assisted development tools, and engineering best practices to accelerate delivery of secure, high-quality software
  • Support integration with legacy air traffic systems and next-generation platform components, including interface definition and troubleshooting
  • Support deployment, operational troubleshooting, and resolution of critical issues in development, test, and production environments
  • Uphold code quality standards, automated testing practices, and peer review discipline within the team
  • Mentor junior engineers and foster collaboration across engineering teams to ensure successful sprint execution and program delivery

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related discipline with 8+ years of relevant experience, or a Master's degree with 6+ years of relevant experience; may also possess a Doctorate. (Equivalent Experience may be used in lieu of degree)
  • 5+ years of experience designing, developing, testing, and reviewing production Java applications
  • 2+ years of experience serving as a Scrum Master on a SAFe Agile team within a large-scale software development environment
  • Experience designing and implementing microservices and RESTful APIs, including JSON, XML, and XSD
  • Significant experience with the Spring Framework, Spring Boot, and Spring Security
  • Experience with unit testing frameworks such as JUnit and Mockito
  • Experience with modern web front-end technologies (React, JavaScript, HTML, CSS)
  • Significant experience with Linux
  • Significant experience with version control systems such as Git
  • Experience with CI/CD pipelines and modern DevOps practices
  • Experience with common development tools and IDEs (IntelliJ, Eclipse, VS Code, etc.)
  • Understanding of sound software development principles and practices
  • Ability to effectively communicate verbally and in writing with both technical and non-technical audiences
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust
  • U.S. citizenship required
  • Successful completion of background investigations as required by the government customer

Preferred Qualifications

  • Knowledge of or experience with AI-assisted coding tools (Claude Code, Codex, etc.)
  • SAFe Scrum Master (SSM), SAFe Advanced Scrum Master (SASM), CSM, or PSM certification
  • Experience with hybrid cloud architectures, data mesh patterns, and cloud-native platform services
  • Experience with containers and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes)
  • Experience with event-driven architectures and messaging (Kafka or equivalent)
  • Knowledge of or experience with the Python programming language
  • Knowledge of or experience with Ansible playbooks and YAML
  • Knowledge of or experience with Linux shell scripting
  • Knowledge of or experience with MongoDB or other NoSQL data stores
  • Knowledge of FedRAMP, FISMA, or government security compliance frameworks
  • Experience with safety-critical or highly regulated software domains
  • Knowledge of air traffic control systems, air traffic management, or flight services
  • Track record of successful delivery on large government programs
  • Desired but not required: Commutable distance to Gaithersburg, MD; Eagan, MN; or Egg Harbor Township, NJ.

Why Leidos?

You’ll work on systems where performance, precision, and reliability matter — every second. This is not experimental AI for prototypes. This is disciplined, responsible AI applied to mission-critical software that supports national infrastructure.

If you’re excited by solving complex problems in regulated, real-world environments — and using AI as a force multiplier rather than a shortcut — we’d like to talk.

title: Technical Project Manager
description:
Technical Project Manager – Systems and Network Integration, Asia Pacific (preferred location Singapore)

Role Purpose:

The Technical Project Manager is responsible for the end-to-end development and delivery of complex security screening, IT network and systems-integration projects throughout the Asia Pacific region. The role combines project management accountability with practical technical capability in the deployment of networked systems, and associated screening, server, storage, workstation, network and edge-device infrastructure.

The successful candidate will lead multidisciplinary teams through requirements definition, detailed planning, site readiness, installation, software integration, configuration, testing, commissioning, customer acceptance and transition to operational support. The role requires an individual who can communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders and who is prepared to take a hands-on role during critical site deployment, integration and acceptance activities.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

1. Responsible for the technical delivery of projects in the Asia Pacific region that contribute to the financial performance of the company.

2. Development of projects involves support and cooperation with primarily the Sales team to identify and define technical solutions, to prepare bids and offers and support in the closure of contracts.

3. Delivery of projects means the successful completion of project deliverables, that is scope, schedule and cost. It also includes the management of Risks, Issues, Assumptions and Dependencies.

4. Manage relationships with customers, sub-contractors, distributors, internal stakeholders and other related parties as necessary.

5. Develop and execute communication plan for each project which includes stakeholders from other countries and therefore at irregular time zones.

6. Ensure that all documentation meets the company’s and contractual requirements.

7. Support the transition and handover from Project to Field Service Support. Including the planning and maintaining of adequate supply of spare parts.

8. Expect to be involved in multiple opportunities and projects of varying size and contribution at one time.

ADDITIONAL TECHNICAL AND DELIVERY RESPONSIBILTIES:

  • Coordinate and, where appropriate, participate directly in equipment installation, software deployment, system configuration, network connectivity verification, software and hardware integration, commissioning and fault investigation.
  • Manage site-readiness activities, including verification of equipment-room availability, rack space, power, uninterruptible power supply requirements, cooling, cabling, fibre connectivity, network ports, IP addressing, access arrangements and operational work windows.
  • Review network and systems designs to identify project dependencies, infrastructure gaps, interface risks, cybersecurity requirements and assumptions that may affect cost, schedule, performance or customer acceptance.
  • Develop and review test plans, test scripts, test evidence, pass/fail criteria, punch lists, defect registers and acceptance certificates.
  • Lead cutover and migration activities for operational systems, including parallel-build arrangements, pilot migrations, phased deployment, rollback planning, change control and coordination with customer operations.
  • Prepare and maintain technical implementation documentation, including Methods of Work, Method Statements, Statements of Work, installation plans, commissioning plans, migration and cutover plans, rollback plans, risk assessments and safe work documentation.

JOB REQUIREMENTS:

· Degree in Engineering, preferably Electronics or Management.

· More than 12 years of work experience, with at least 6 years of project management and people management experience with an international organization.

· Prior experience in management of capital equipment / systems projects or programs.

· Proven ownership of project scope, budget and schedule and the ability to demonstrate it.

· Proven experience handing projects or programs with contract value in excess of SGD 1 million would be an advantage.

· PMP or PRINCE2 certification would be an desirable.

· Experience with aviation security screening systems, baggage-handling or hold-baggage screening environments, X-ray or CT screening equipment, building control systems, industrial control systems or other integrated electromechanical systems.

· Demonstrated practical experience delivering enterprise IT, operational technology or mission-critical networked systems, including installation, integration, testing, commissioning and operational handover.

· Strong working knowledge of network infrastructure and architecture, including Ethernet switching, TCP/IP, IP addressing, subnetting, VLANs, routing fundamentals, fibre and copper connectivity, redundancy, network segmentation, firewalls, servers, virtualised environments, storage and edge-connected devices.

· Ability to read, understand and review high-level and low-level system architecture diagrams, network topology diagrams, rack layouts, cable schedules, interface-control documentation and system configuration information.

· Experience in multiple stakeholder management with an ability to plan and execute a stakeholder management strategy.

· Experience in high-reliability or mission-critical, "24x7" environment similar to Aviation industry.

· Excellent organizational skills

· Team player with the ability to prioritize and work under pressure in a fast-paced environment with minimal supervision.

· Good interpersonal skills and the ability to manage varying levels of customers and company personnel and get things done through people.

· Ability to travel within Asia, sometimes at short notice
