title: Flight Software Development Lead
description:
The Huntsville Defense Sector Engineering Matrix in the Leidos Defense Sector currently has a special job opening for a talented Flight and Mission Software Development Lead to work onsite in our Huntsville, AL office. This is an exciting and unusual opportunity to use your knowledge, skills, experience, and insight to launch the next phase of your career at Leidos by leading a talented software team through the software development life cycle (SDLC) to produce solutions for the nation’s leading advanced defense technologies such as manned aircraft software, tactical strike systems, sensors, computer vision, uncrewed air systems (UAS), counter UAS, mission planning, command/control/communications (C3), platform autonomy, network collaborative autonomy, aerial refueling, and flight management systems.

Leidos is dedicated to making the world a safer place. This starts with helping our customers in the Defense Industry achieve their critical missions. Our dedicated Defense Group employees are solving critical challenges across the globe. At Leidos, we deliver innovative solutions through the efforts of our diverse and talented people who are dedicated to our customers’ success. We empower our teams, contribute to our communities, and operate sustainably. Everything we do is built on a commitment to do the right thing for our customers, our people, and our community. Our Mission, Vision, and Values guide the way we do business. With offices across the United States engaging in the defense, space, cyber and commercial fields, Leidos provides responsive, cost-effective engineering, scientific and IT solutions. Leidos is well known for our people-oriented culture, positive work environment, technical excellence, and resilient business ethics.

Primary Responsibilities.

  • This leadership position is dynamic, requiring assertiveness, strong technical competence, flexibility, impeccable prioritization abilities, personal drive and energy, and self-discipline. Working in this position, your workday will span jobs such as leading a Software Integrated Product Team (IPT), working across technical functions on cohesive integrated solutions on complex integrated systems, providing software program management, working closely with software and computing hardware architects, overseeing software systems engineers and lead software test engineers, and serving as Agile Product Owner.

  • Product development will span the technology stack from high-level user applications to mission software to low-level embedded solutions to the computing hardware. Hardware may span front end tablets and laptops, rugged mission computers, high-performance servers, single-board computers (SBC), systems-on-chip (SoC), systems-on-module (SoM), custom printed circuit board assemblies (PCBA), and microcontrollers (MCU). Software capabilities span criticality levels and perform functions such as mission execution, power and thermal monitoring, sensors and instrumentation, telemetry, command and control, communications, networks, mission planning, and system infrastructures.

  • This position will involve regular and direct contributions to proposals. This includes devising technical solutions, determining the approach to execution, schedule planning, software size and cost estimation, developing basis of estimates, team sizing, skills and staff planning, computer hardware and software requirements elicitation and analysis, and materiel planning.

  • Direct communication with customers, end users, internal stakeholders, and team members will be required on a frequent basis.

  • In this position you will enjoy significant influence on positive outcomes and a strong sense of purpose working directly on fieldable systems that are key to the nation’s defense.

Basic Qualifications.

  • A Bachelor's Degree or higher degree in Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Management Information Systems, Computer Information Systems, Electrical Engineering, Aeronautical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, or a related technical field is required.

  • Candidate should have 12+ years of relevant technical experience.

  • Candidate should have 3+ years or relevant experience leading teams and managing resources for software development.

  • Excellent communication (verbal and written) and team leadership skills.

  • Candidate must demonstrate their ability to work independently, collaborate closely with team members, discern efficient roles and tasks for their team members, think critically, act confidently and judiciously, exercise impeccable judgement, consistently make rational decisions, and impart a productive sense of urgency to others.

  • Experience in development of software products or simulations using C, C++, Rust, C#, or Java is required. Candidate must articulate strong competency in development in at least one of these programming languages, object-oriented design principles, and troubleshooting.

  • Experience working on one or more final products that went beyond prototypes, demonstrations, test beds, or internal/lab use only. The candidate’s prior experience must exist on software products, integrated systems, or simulations that were released and fielded as either a product itself, used operationally on an integrated system, or released and used independently by individuals other than those who developed it.

  • Proficient with efficient use of peer reviews and evaluations of software development plans, specifications, requirements management, architectures, designs, source code, unit tests, verification plans and procedures.

  • Familiar with practices associated with successful software supplier or subcontractor management, and basic contract requirements methodology (e.g., SOWs, SLAs, and CDRLs).

  • Fundamental and working knowledge of software configuration management, code repositories and build system components, such as DevSecOps, CI/CD pipelines, CMake, GitLab, Docker, and virtualization tools (e.g., VMWare, QEMU, VirtualBox, Hyper-V).

  • Fundamental and working knowledge of general-purpose operating systems (Linux, UNIX, and/or Windows) and practical knowledge of their respective development tools/IDEs, scripts, debuggers, and administrative features.

  • Understanding of the software development life cycle, its phases, life cycle models, metrics or performance indicators, and techniques for rapid development while ensuring high-quality solutions and on-time results.

  • Able to multi-task and willing to work with teammates to contribute directly to industry events, white papers and competitive proposals.

  • Basic understanding of software engineering process and the appropriateness of its use, application, and proper methods of tailoring.

  • Basic understanding of systems engineering principles and practices relevant to software.

Clearance Qualification.

  • Candidate must be a U.S. Citizen with the ability to obtain and maintain a Secret Security Clearance (interim and final).

Preferred Experience, Skills or Abilities.

  • Software Development: Experience with planning, specification, design, development, integration, installation/deployment, and maintenance of software for airborne systems, mission planning systems, missile/weapon platforms, uncrewed or autonomous systems, and/or ground control/support systems.

  • User Experience Programming Languages: Basic knowledge in one or more programming languages used in applications and front-end software, such as Python, .NET/C#, Java, C++, Qt, Swift/Objective-C, and XML.

  • Agile Development: Experience with SAFe as Product Owner, Scrum Master, or Developer performing software product development using Agile development methodologies within one or more Agile tools such as Atlassian Jira, Trello, Monday.com.

  • Agentic AI: Experience using and influencing the adoption of tools like Anthropic’s Claude Code, OpenAI’s Codex or other coding agents to improve efficiency and productivity.

  • Problem-Solving: Ability to comprehend changes, characterize impact and assess risk to plans or existing solutions, estimate their level of effort and resources, describe (written and verbal) courses of action (COA) or decision analysis, and facilitate team consensus.

  • Collaboration: Work responsibly, reliably and independently in a fast-paced, open, collaborative cross-functional cross-organizational environment without direct oversight.

  • Transparency: Elicit, accept, and provide constructive informal feedback amongst other team members to uphold technical excellence and quality workmanship.

Other Qualifications

  • Rapid Flight Systems Development. Experience with Agile/Scrum, unmanned aircraft or robotics, embedded development, design and implementation of operational flight software, digital communications, real-time development, and software safety.

  • Qualification Testing. Knowledge of various development tools for software qualification testing, requirements management, build and release, unit testing, regression testing, configuration management, and issue tracking are beneficial.

  • Mission Support: Devise new concepts for computing infrastructure and automation to support ground test facilities, integration labs, data collection and analysis, autonomous logistics, and operator training.

  • Embedded Software: Understanding of fundamentals of critical or time-sensitive software for integrated systems, such as real-time software, hardware-in-the-loop simulation, vehicles, medical devices, or IoT components.

  • Specialized Areas: Experience with autonomous systems, electrical and software interface design, interface control documents, or avionics is beneficial.

title: ABA Student Analyst - Little Rock
description:
Are you a compassionate and enthusiastic person looking to positively impact the lives of children diagnosed with special needs? At Pediatrics Plus you can do just that! We are currently seeking ABA Student Analysts to join our team of highly qualified professionals that share our vision of Empowering Children to Conquer their World! Pediatrics Plus is a highly collaborative pediatric healthcare provider. We are committed to helping children succeed in all stages of life through evidence-based therapy (Applied Behavior Analysis, Occupational Therapy, Physical Therapy, and Speech Therapy) and developmental preschool services, state of the art facilities, specialized equipment, family support and education, and community investment.

Why you’ll love working at Pediatrics Plus:

  • Competitive Pay Compensation
  • Paid Time Off, Benefits, and 401K
  • Training & Development
  • Personal Growth & Leadership Opportunities
  • Supportive & Interdisciplinary Work Environment

What you will do:

The ABA Student Analyst will provide an unique opportunity for a graduate student pursuing certification as a Board-Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) to gain hands-on experience in both direct service delivery as an RBT and in the fieldwork required for BCBA certification. The individual will work directly with individuals with autism and other developmental disabilities while simultaneously engaging in required fieldwork hours under the supervision of a licensed BCBA. This dual role offers valuable experience in both practical behavior intervention and the application of ABA principles to gain skills needed for an entry-level BCBA.

  • Assist in conducting functional behavior assessments (FBAs), preference assessments, and other relevant assessments under the guidance of a BCBA.
  • Participate in the development and modification of behavior intervention plans (BIPs), treatment goals, and individualized service plans, ensuring they align with client needs and evidence-based practices under the supervision of the BCBA.
  • Collect, record, and analyze data related to client behaviors, treatment progress, and session outcomes. Prepare data reports and assist in modifying treatment plans based on data analysis.
  • Attend regular clinical supervision meetings with a BCBA or clinical supervisor to review client progress, receive feedback, and develop professional competencies required for BCBA certification.
  • Assist in case documentation by maintaining detailed and accurate client records, including progress notes, treatment plans, and other documentation in accordance with company policies and ethical guidelines.
  • Provide one-on-one direct behavioral intervention to clients in home, clinic, and/or community settings. Implement behavior intervention plans (BIPs) and training programs as designed by the BCBA.
  • Implement skill-building programs designed to teach clients new skills, including communication, social, academic, and daily living skills according to the Individualized Treatment Plan (ITP) for skill acquisition.
  • Implement behavior reduction strategies, including reinforcement, prompting, and other interventions to reduce challenging behaviors according to the Individualized Treatment Plan (ITP).
  • Accurately collect data on client behaviors, progress, and skill acquisition during therapy sessions. Ensure data is taken in real-time and is consistent with the goals outlined in treatment plans.
  • Collaborate with family members, caregivers, and other team members to ensure consistency and generalization of skills across settings. Provide guidance to families regarding behavior management strategies and client progress.
  • Adhere to the ethical guidelines outlined by the Behavior Analyst Certification Board (BACB) and maintain professionalism in all interactions with clients, families, and team members.
  • Represent the program to parents, visitors, and the public in a positive way.
  • Ensure confidentiality of children and employee information. Respond to internal and external requests for information according to clinic policy.
  • Participate in one-on-one meetings with leader.
  • Comply with BACB’s ethics requirements.
Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Minimum Requirements:

  • Current certification of Registered Behavior Technician through the Behavior Analyst Certification Board (BACB).
  • Current graduate student within an ABA program seeking certification as a Board-Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) for a minimum of 6 months.

What you have:

  • Ability to communicate effectively and professionally with a wide variety of people.
  • Ability to work with children birth to age 21 and families who are at risk.
  • Strong organizational skills with attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Ability to handle multiple tasks in a very busy environment.
  • Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, policies, and other company documents.
  • Ability to author routine reports and correspondence.
  • Ability to apply common sense understanding to carry out instructions furnished in written, oral, or diagram form.
  • Reports for work dressed appropriately and complies with company policies regarding the dress code.
  • Ability to maintain regular and punctual attendance.
  • Ability to complete tasks in a timely manner.

Physical Demands:

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to accurately communicate information and ideas so others will understand through sight and hearing. The employee is regularly required to move including walking, running, jumping, and sitting. The employee is regularly required to use hands and fingers to handle, lift, reach, and feel. The employee is frequently required to stand and stoop, twist, bend, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include near and distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus. The employee must be comfortable around standard farm animals, including minimal allergies to touching, smelling, feeding, and engaging with animals.

description:
Who are We?

Brooke Charter Schools is a network of four public charter schools, serving grades K-12 in Mattapan, Roslindale, and East Boston. At Brooke, we coach and invest in our teachers so that they can help our students achieve at the highest levels and graduate from college. We believe academic achievement empowers our students to live choice-filled lives and enhances their ability to contribute to creating a just world. In a culture of achievement, educators support students in recognizing and building on their identities as sources of strength even as they work to grow and achieve in new ways.

What is the School Psychologist Role?

As a school psychologist at Brooke, you provide direct support to individual and small groups of students in the areas of social skills, self-regulation, self-advocacy, etc and create and implement positive behavioral plans. You collaborate with stakeholders including serving as a liaison between the school, student, parent, and external agencies, as well as engaging parents and teachers as partners in students' therapeutic interventions. title: Senior Fixed Income Analyst
description:
About This Job

The Senior Fixed Income Analyst is responsible for conducting in-depth credit research and analysis across corporate and municipal fixed income securities while supporting portfolio manager decision-making across fixed income SMAs. Leveraging advanced experience across corporate, municipal, and structured products markets, this role independently conducts deep fundamental, market, and economic research; develops investment theses; and provides high-conviction recommendations to portfolio managers. These recommendations include issuer-specific guidance and portfolio parameter changes, both of which directly impact day-to-day trading activities across a $2 billion portfolio. The role works directly with financial advisors to support end-client conversations, participates in portfolio positioning and the creation of new strategies, and additionally executes trades across client portfolios with precision, market awareness, and product expertise.

It is anticipated that an incumbent in this role will work as a Hybrid employee, with three (3) or more days each week required on-site at one of the listed office locations.

Candidates should be located within a commutable distance to an office. Internal candidates currently aligned to an Orion office location may be given preference; however, internal candidates with varying work arrangements may be considered based on experience and business needs. Work location is subject to change based on business needs.

Essential Functions of the Job

  • Conduct independent, in-depth research on corporate issuers, including financial analysis, sector assessments, and structural evaluation.

  • Conduct detailed analysis of state and local municipal government finances, pension obligations, tax-base trends, revenue sources, and debt structures.

  • Provide buy/hold/sell recommendations on corporate and municipal issuers.

  • Place corporate, treasury, municipal, structured product, and agency trades across client portfolios, ensuring accuracy, compliance alignment, and efficient implementation of portfolio strategy.

  • Partner with financial advisors by delivering fixed income market insights, product knowledge, and credit perspectives to support end-client conversations.

  • Lead the development and maintenance of municipal and corporate credit frameworks, sector outlooks, and approved issuer lists.

  • Monitor municipal and corporate market developments and provide regular credit updates to portfolio managers and advisors.

  • Serve as a primary research partner to portfolio managers in portfolio construction and sector allocation decisions.

  • Provide recommendations regarding portfolio positioning, duration management, sector weighting, and credit allocation.

  • Participate in investment strategy discussions and contribute to strategic portfolio decisions.

  • Serve as lead researcher on the buildout of new strategies.

  • Mentor and train Fixed Income Analysts on credit research methodologies, municipal and corporate analysis, and fixed income market fundamentals.

  • Represent the credit committee in advisor meetings, client reviews, and market update presentations.

  • Create fixed income content for internal audiences, advisors, and end clients.

  • Identify and implement process improvements that increase research efficiency and scalability.

Skills Needed to Perform the Job

  • Advanced credit analysis skills, including financial statement analysis, leverage and coverage ratios, cash flow modeling, and covenant evaluation across corporate issuers.

  • Deep expertise in municipal finance, including state and local government budgets, tax-base trends, pension and OPEB liabilities, revenue sources, and general obligation bond structures.

  • Strong relative value and structured product analysis skills across corporate, municipal, and structured fixed income sectors.

  • Proficiency in portfolio construction principles, including duration management, yield curve positioning, and sector and credit allocation specific to SMAs.

  • Sound judgment in OTC fixed income trading, including bond pricing, liquidity assessment, and best-execution practices.

  • Strong proficiency with fixed income analytics platforms, such as Bloomberg, and financial modeling in Excel.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex credit analysis into clear guidance for portfolio managers, advisors, and clients.

  • Demonstrated ability to mentor junior analysts and drive process improvements that scale research efficiency.

  • Experience in product development or strategy design.

Board Collaboration, Capital Investment, Client-Centric, Effective Communication, Financial Management, Fixed Income Investments, Innovation, Inspirational Communication, Investment Management, Managed Accounts, Market Liquidity, Organizational Diplomacy, Organizational Vision, Strategic Risk Management, Technical Proficiency, Time Management, Work Collaboratively

At Orion, we achieve our best work when we support one another, staying personally accountable to each other and the clients we serve. title: Electrical Contract Engineering Lead
description:
At Amentum, we're not just solving problems; we're engineering the future. Our team is driven by an unyielding commitment to innovation, integrity, and collaboration, tackling some of the most significant challenges in science, security, and sustainability. If you're passionate about making a real impact and want to be part of a community that values ethical excellence, this is the place where your ambition can thrive.

Here, we believe that success comes from continuously pushing boundaries and working together to deliver on our promises. We embrace challenges with confidence and are dedicated to creating a secure and vibrant future for all.

We’ll inspire and empower you to deliver your best work so you can evolve, grow and succeed – today and into tomorrow. We offer an exciting range of opportunities to develop your career within a supportive team who always strive to do the right thing for our people, clients and communities.

People are our greatest asset, and we offer a competitive package to retain and attract the best talent.

In addition to the benefits you’d expect, UK employees also receive free single medical cover and digital GP service, family-friendly benefits such as enhanced parental leave pay and free membership of employee assistance and parental programmes, plus reimbursement towards relevant professional development and memberships.

Work-life balance and flexibility is a key focus area for us. We’re happy to discuss hybrid, part-time and flexible working hours, patterns and locations to suit you and our business.

About the Opportunity

We employ the UK's most experienced and skilled technical services professionals and has grown to over 8,000 people in locations across the UK - we provide the resources to turn great ideas into reality, and we offer capable and committed individuals the opportunity to shape their careers how they wish.

Hinkley Point C (HPC) is the first new nuclear power station to be built in the UK in over 20 years, HPCs two EPR reactors will be capable of generating 3.26GW of secure, low carbon electricity for 60 years, enough electricity to power around 6 million homes. In addition to the projects ‘clean energy’ benefits, HPC will create thousands of jobs and bring lasting benefits to the UK economy.

The Electrical Contract Engineering Lead will act as the engineering lead within EPR-E for one or more electrical equipment contracts supporting the Hinkley Point C (HPC) and Sizewell C (SZC) programmes.


The role is responsible for coordinating and managing the delivery of the associated design and qualification packages, providing engineering oversight of supplier activities and ensuring technical deliverables are progressed to the required quality, programme and engineering standards.


The Contract Engineering Lead operates with a high degree of autonomy, coordinating technical specialists and acting as a key interface between EPR-E, NNB equipment programme teams and other engineering stakeholders.


Key Responsibilities

  • Act as Engineering Lead for assigned electrical equipment contracts, with overall accountability for delivery of the associated design and qualification package.
  • Lead the technical review of supplier documentation, including management of document review workflows and oversight of the quality and consistency of reviews completed by other technical specialists.
  • Undertake technical reviews directly where appropriate.
  • Coordinate input from EPR-E technical specialists, ensuring that specialist activities support the wider contract design and qualification programme.
  • Monitor engineering progress, risks and emerging technical issues across assigned contracts.
  • Provide regular progress and issue reporting to the NNB Project Manager and EPR-E management team.
  • Liaise with the NNB Equipment Programme and other engineering stakeholders to resolve design and qualification matters.
  • Participate in contract-specific weekly and monthly progress meetings.
  • Represent assigned contracts during the weekly EGD team meeting and provide updates to EPR-E management.
  • Plan, coordinate and complete engineering surveillance activities.
  • Produce the annual surveillance summary report.
  • Maintain, review and update the Contract Surveillance Programme.
  • Identify issues requiring escalation and coordinate resolution through senior management, technical authorities or company experts where required

Qualifications Skills & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree, or equivalent qualification, in Electrical Engineering or another relevant engineering discipline
  • Experience working as an electrical engineer within industrial applications
  • Experience of industrial electrical power distribution systems
  • Experience working within a highly regulated or safety-critical engineering environment
  • Experience reviewing and assuring technical engineering documentation
  • Ability to coordinate technical activities and inputs from multiple engineering specialists
  • Experience managing technical interfaces and stakeholders across complex organisations
  • Ability to operate independently, prioritise workload and progress technical issues with limited supervision

Previous nuclear industry experience is not essential. Relevant transferable experience could include industries such as:
Oil and gas, conventional or renewable power generation, aerospace, defence and any other safety-critical or heavily regulated engineering sectors.

Our Culture

Our values are built on a strong foundation of safety, integrity, and respect for every individual. People are at the heart of our mission, and we believe in supporting one another through a culture of care and collaboration.

We strive to create a workplace where everyone feels they belong and can thrive. Supporting mental wellbeing and fostering a sense of connection are essential to how we work.

When we embrace different perspectives and work together, we become more innovative, more agile, and more successful.

description:

JOB SUMMARY:

The City of Birmingham is seeking a well-qualified and motivated Senior Planner to join their Hazard Mitigation Division. Senior Planners focus on reviewing submission documents such as drawings, maps, surveys, and applications related to development projects to ensure compliance with City and department requirements and ordinances. Individuals in this job class also act as liaisons for the department to various committees, commissions, and citizens to communicate activities taking place, and to provide information related to project development within the community. Their work is performed under the general direction of a supervisor and is reviewed for completeness and adherence to policies and procedures.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS:

The City of Birmingham provides competitive pay and comprehensive benefits packages to include medical and dental insurance, employer-sponsored retirement plan (pension), generous paid holidays, sick and vacation leave, and more. The pay range for this job is listed below:

$60,486 - $93,828

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

The following are job-related qualifications that are required for employment consideration for this position:

Option A:

  • Driver's license.

  • Experience writing, developing, or preparing hazard mitigation plans and long-range planning elements, such as land-use planning, environmental planning, and demographics.

  • Experience collecting and analyzing data (e.g., demographic, land-use survey, market, census) in preparation for a planning study.

  • Experience writing, developing, preparing, and interpreting current planning functions or development regulations, including zoning, subdivision, and floodplain regulations.

  • Experience implementing long-range, short-range plans and hazard mitigation plans and developing appropriate regulations to specific situations.

  • Experience developing and delivering presentations to the public, public bodies, and other stakeholders (e.g., civic and business organizations, neighborhood associations, public hearings).

Option B:

  • Driver's license.

  • Bachelor's degree in Planning, Urban Planning, Emergency Management, Urban Studies, Public Administration, Environmental Management, or a related degree.

  • Experience writing, developing, or preparing hazard mitigation plans and/or long-range planning elements, such as land-use planning, environmental planning, and demographics.

  • Experience developing and delivering presentations to the public, public bodies, and other stakeholders (e.g., civic and business organizations, neighborhood associations, public hearings).

TYPICAL JOB DUTIES:

  • Reviews drawings, maps, surveys, and applications for various purposes (e.g., zoning, subdivisions, building, addressing, construction permits) to ensure compliance with departmental requirements and County/City codes and ordinances.

  • Communicates with various individuals (e.g., contractors, realtors, engineers, developers, general public) in order to answer questions and explain ordinances relating to flood plain, zoning, signage, subdivision, future land use, and the comprehension plan.

  • Processes cases or projects (e.g., re-zoning cases, subdivision cases, variances) by conducting research, analysis, and findings of cases in order to ensure accuracy and adherence to best planning practices.

  • Acts as a staff liaison to various committees/commissions (e.g., Planning and Zoning Commission, Zoning Board of Adjustment, Subdivision Committee, Zoning Advisory Committee, Historic Preservation, Planning and Zoning, Design Review Board, Board of Landscape Design) in order to gather feedback, relay information and deliver presentations.

  • Participates in strategic, current, and long-range planning and ordinance revisions by conducting research and analyzing various data (e.g., demographic reports, neighborhood revitalization plans) to ensure compliance with federal and state regulations.

  • Manages federal and state project-based grants to include defining and managing the project scope and deliverables, troubleshooting problem areas, and overseeing project budgets, timelines and contingency plans.

  • Manages hazard mitigation and/or disaster recovery programs and watershed and/or floodplain planning programs by developing management plans, protocols, and procedures to ensure compliance with state and federal regulations and requirements.

  • Researches other adopted city or county long-range plans to ensure the site development plans/projects are consistent with the stated goals of the long-range plan.

  • Reviews site and development plans for adherence to development regulations required through the Zoning Ordinance and, when appropriate, approves them.

  • Conducts or participates in neighborhood or public involvement meetings to inform citizens about projects in their community and to obtain feedback.

  • Interprets codes and ordinances to ensure compliance with applicable federal regulations and programs.

Work is conducted mostly indoors in an office setting, with periodic field visits to external indoor or outdoor locations. Work involves use of standard office equipment, such as computer, phone, copier, etc.

title: Hospital Based Patient Advocate
description:
Make a real difference in patients’ lives—join Elevate Patient Financial Solutions as a Hospital Based Patient Advocate and help guide individuals through their healthcare financial journey. This full-time position is located 100% onsite at a hospital in Nampa, ID, with a Monday-Friday schedule from 9:00am-5:30pm.

Bring your passion for helping others and grow with a company that values your impact. In 2024, our Advocates helped over 823,000 patients secure the Medicaid coverage they needed. Elevate’s mission is to make a difference. Are you ready to be the difference?

As a Hospital Based Patient Advocate, you play a vital role in guiding uninsured hospital patients through the complex landscape of medical and disability assistance. This onsite, hospital-based role places you at the heart of patient financial advocacy—meeting individuals face-to-face, right in their hospital rooms, to guide them through the process of identifying eligibility and applying for financial assistance. Your presence and empathy make a real difference during some of life’s most vulnerable moments.

Job Summary

The purpose of this position is to connect uninsured hospital patients to programs that will cover their medical expenses. As a Patient Advocate, you will play a critical role in assisting uninsured hospital patients by evaluating their eligibility for various federal, state, and county medical or disability assistance programs through bed-side visits and in-person interactions. Your primary objective will be to guide patients face-to-face through the application process, ensuring thorough completion and follow-up. This role is crucial in ensuring that uninsured patients are promptly identified and assisted, with the goal of meeting our benchmark that 98% of patients are screened at bedside.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities
  • Screen uninsured hospital patients at bedside in an effort to determine if patient is a viable candidate for federal, state, and/or county medical or disability assistance.
  • Complete the appropriate applications and following through until approved.
  • Detailed, accurate and timely documentation in both Elevate PFS and hospital systems on all cases worked.
  • Provide exceptional customer service skills at all times.
  • Maintain assigned work queue of patient accounts.
  • Collaborate in person and through verbal/written correspondence with hospital staff, case managers, social workers, financial counselors.
  • Answer incoming telephone calls, make out-bound calls, and track all paperwork necessary to submit enrollment and renewal for prospective Medicaid patients.
  • Maintain structured and timely contact with the applicant and responsible government agency, by phone whenever possible or as structured via the daily work queue.
  • Assist the applicant with gathering any additional reports or records, meeting appointment dates and times and arrange transportation if warranted.
  • Conduct in-person community visits as needed to acquire documentation.
  • As per established protocols, inform the client in a timely manner of all approvals and denials of coverage.
  • Attend ongoing required training to remain informed about current rules and regulations related to governmental programs, and apply updated knowledge when working with patients and cases.
  • Regular and timely attendance.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Requirements

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or abilities.
  • Some college coursework preferred
  • Prior hospital experience preferred
  • Adaptability when dealing with constantly changing processes, computer systems and government programs
  • Professional experience working with state and federal programs
  • Critical thinking skills
  • Ability to maneuver throughout the hospital and patients’ rooms throughout scheduled work shift.
  • Proficient experience utilizing Microsoft Office Suite with emphasis on Excel and Outlook
  • Effectively communicate both orally and written, to a variety of individuals
  • Ability to multitask to meet performance metrics while functioning in a fast-paced environment.
  • Hospital-Based Patient Advocates are expected to dress in accordance with their respective Client’s Dress Code.
  • Hybrid positions require home internet connections that meet the Company’s upload and download speed criteria. Hybrid employees working from home are expected to comply with Elevate’s Remote Work Policy, including but not limited to working in a private and dedicated workspace where confidential information can be shared in accordance with HIPAA and PHI requirements.
Benefits
ElevatePFS believes in making a positive impact not only within our industry but also with our employees –the organization’s greatest asset! We take pride in offering comprehensive benefits in a vast array of plans that contribute to the present and future well-being of our employees and their families.
  • Medical, Dental & Vision Insurance

description:
The University of Mississippi — fondly referred to as Ole Miss — stands as a premier public research institution with a proud legacy of academic distinction. We are devoted to nurturing a vibrant, inclusive community where every member — student, faculty, and staff — can achieve their fullest potential.

Join the Ole Miss Family — Build Your Legacy Here!

Job Summary:

The Director of the University of Mississippi Field Station (UMFS) provides strategic leadership and operational oversight for a 700-acre living laboratory consisting of diverse ecosystems, including mixed forests, grasslands, wetlands, springs, streams, and more than 220 lakes and ponds. The facility also includes research laboratories, office space, and other infrastructure that support interdisciplinary environmental research and education.

The Director is responsible for managing the overall operations of the field station, including supervision of two to three staff members, budget administration, facility maintenance, and ensuring that research and educational resources are well-equipped, accessible, and effectively maintained. The position plays a critical role in advancing the UMFS mission by fostering a collaborative environment that supports high-impact ecological and environmental sciences research.

Working with university leadership, faculty, students, and external partners, the Director will strengthen the field station's role as a premier center for ecosystem stewardship and environmental discovery. The successful candidate will ensure that all aspects of UMFS operations align with and support its three core mission areas: education, research, and outreach, while enhancing the station's visibility, impact, and service to the university and broader community.

Job Description:

  • Engages UM scientists and students to encourage use of UMFS for research and teaching activities with appropriate oversight (i.e. IACUC, IRB, Lab Safety)
  • Works with partners and collaborators to design, coordinate, and enhance outreach programs.

  • Seeks funding to support and grow summer camps and outreach activities for K-12 students and the public.
  • Establishes guidelines and policies to ensure UMFS facilities and properties are maintained in concert with long-term strategic plans.
  • Creates and maintains partnerships with internal and external partners. Meets with target stakeholder groups to assess needs and gain input on plans for UMFS.
  • Researches and identifies potential funding sources for infrastructure improvements.
  • Develops and submits proposals for infrastructure improvements and broad-based science activities.
  • Partners with scientists to identify opportunities in which they may tap for UMFS-based projects.
  • Oversees and manages fiscal activities of the UMFS budget and affiliated grants and contracts.
  • Provides supervision and guidance to UMFS staff.
  • Encourages the use of the facilities for leisure activities such as picnicking, hiking, photography, fishing, and trail running.

title: NEN Solution Engineering – Sr. Voice Engineer
description:
We are seeking a seasoned, hands-on Senior VoIP, VTC, and Telephony Solution Engineer to support the design, integration, validation, deployment, and sustainment of enterprise Unified Communications and Collaboration solutions.

Reporting to the Voice/VTC Manager, this position will serve as a senior technical contributor and may act as the technical lead for assigned projects, workstreams, or engineering efforts. The engineer will be responsible for developing solutions to complex technical problems that span multiple systems or disciplines and for helping ensure assigned solutions are secure, resilient, supportable, and operationally ready.

The engineer may provide technical direction, coordinate the work of engineers supporting an assigned project, review engineering products, and mentor less-experienced team members, but will not be responsible for employee performance management, staffing decisions, or organizational workforce planning.

The successful candidate will remain actively engaged in requirements analysis, alternatives analysis, solution architecture, detailed design, laboratory validation, implementation planning, system integration, testing, and Tier 3/Tier 4 engineering escalations. The position will work closely with Transport Engineering, Network Operations, Cybersecurity, program leadership, customers, telecommunications carriers, and technology vendors.

Key Responsibilities

1. Technical Project and Workstream Leadership

  • Technical Execution: Lead the technical planning and execution of assigned VoIP, VTC, telephony, and collaboration projects or workstreams.
  • Project Coordination: Coordinate engineering activities across multiple technical areas, identify dependencies, track technical milestones, and support the timely completion of project deliverables.
  • Technical Direction: Provide technical guidance to engineers assigned to a project, review engineering work products, and help resolve technical issues that could affect cost, schedule, performance, or operational readiness.
  • Risk Management: Identify technical risks, constraints, assumptions, and dependencies and recommend practical mitigation approaches to project and engineering leadership.
  • Estimating and Planning: Support the development of engineering estimates, bills of material, staffing assumptions, implementation schedules, and levels of effort.
  • Technical Mentoring: Mentor and support other engineers through design reviews, peer reviews, troubleshooting activities, and knowledge-sharing sessions.

2. Systems Engineering and Solution Lifecycle

  • Requirements Analysis: Analyze operational, functional, technical, cybersecurity, performance, availability, and supportability requirements for assigned solutions.
  • Alternatives and Trade Studies: Evaluate technical alternatives based on capability, cost, risk, interoperability, lifecycle status, security, supportability, and implementation complexity.
  • Requirements Allocation: Translate customer and program requirements into system, subsystem, interface, configuration, and testing requirements.
  • Solution Documentation: Develop and maintain high-level designs, low-level designs, interface definitions, bills of material, configuration baselines, implementation procedures, rollback plans, test plans, and as-built documentation.
  • Verification and Validation: Plan and perform laboratory validation, interoperability testing, system testing, acceptance testing, and other verification activities needed to confirm that solutions satisfy defined requirements.
  • Configuration and Quality Control: Apply established engineering, cybersecurity, configuration-management, and quality-assurance processes throughout the solution lifecycle.
  • Operational Transition: Support the transition of new or modified solutions to operations by confirming that monitoring, documentation, support procedures, training requirements, and operational dependencies have been addressed.

3. Voice, Video, and Collaboration Solution Engineering

  • Solution Design: Design and integrate enterprise voice, video teleconferencing, Session Initiation Protocol, Session Border Controller, telephony, and collaboration solutions.
  • Enterprise Telephony: Engineer enterprise dial plans, E.164 number normalization, digit manipulation, call routing, SIP trunking, carrier interconnections, PSTN services, voice gateways, voicemail, and emergency-calling capabilities.
  • VTC and Collaboration: Design and integrate multi-vendor VTC and audiovisual collaboration environments, including Cisco Room Series and Webex devices, Poly, Microsoft Teams Rooms, Crestron, Zoom Rooms, and comparable technologies.
  • Cloud and Hybrid Integration: Develop integrations between on-premises voice infrastructure and cloud collaboration platforms such as Microsoft Teams Phone, Direct Routing, Operator Connect, Webex Calling, and comparable services.
  • Availability and Resiliency: Develop technical requirements and designs for high availability, geographic redundancy, survivability, disaster recovery, capacity management, and service continuity.
  • Technology Evaluation: Conduct product evaluations, proof-of-concept activities, interoperability testing, and technical risk assessments for new or replacement voice, video, and collaboration technologies.
  • Technical Roadmaps: Contribute technical analysis, lifecycle data, recommendations, and implementation considerations to technology-modernization and product-roadmap activities.

4. Hands-On Engineering and Technical Escalation

  • Configuration and Deployment: Configure, integrate, test, and deploy IP telephony systems, SIP proxies, voice gateways, Session Border Controllers, VTC systems, and unified communications platforms.
  • Session Border Controllers: Configure and troubleshoot enterprise SBC technologies, including AudioCodes, Ribbon, Cisco CUBE, Oracle Communications Session Border Controller/Acme Packet, or comparable platforms.
  • Complex Troubleshooting: Resolve complex voice and video problems involving call routing, signaling, media negotiation, interoperability, packet loss, jitter, latency, one-way audio, call quality, and service availability.
  • Root-Cause Analysis: Perform detailed technical investigations, identify underlying causes, develop corrective actions, and document lessons learned.
  • QoS and Transport Integration: Collaborate with Transport and Network Engineering to design and validate end-to-end Quality of Service, including DSCP and Layer 2 Class of Service marking, queuing, shaping, policing, call-admission control, bandwidth planning, and class-of-service mapping.
  • Network Analysis: Evaluate routing, switching, VLAN, firewall, Network Address Translation, DNS, certificate, and transport conditions that affect voice and video services.
  • Monitoring and Service Assurance: Support monitoring, alerting, call-quality analytics, call-detail records, capacity reporting, and trend analysis for enterprise voice and video services.

5. Stakeholder and Vendor Coordination

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work with Transport Engineering, Network Operations, Cybersecurity, program management, customers, and operations personnel to align technical solutions with infrastructure, security, and operational requirements.
  • Technical Communication: Explain technical issues, risks, alternatives, and recommendations to engineers, project leaders, client team members, and other stakeholders.
  • Design Reviews: Lead or participate in technical interchange meetings, peer reviews, architecture reviews, test-readiness reviews, and implementation-readiness reviews.
  • Vendor Coordination: Coordinate technical activities with equipment manufacturers, software providers, telecommunications carriers, SIP service providers, subcontractors, and system integrators.
  • Technical Influence: Develop well-supported technical recommendations and work with project and engineering leaders to gain acceptance of proposed designs, processes, or corrective actions.

Required Experience and Education

  • Professional Experience: Typically requires a bachelor’s degree and 8–12 years of relevant experience, or a master’s degree and 6–10 years of relevant experience. Equivalent relevant education, certifications, and practical experience may be considered.
  • Technical Background: Progressive engineering experience in VoIP, VTC, enterprise telephony, unified communications, collaboration systems, networking, or a closely related technical discipline.
  • Project Leadership: Demonstrated experience leading the technical execution of complex projects, workstreams, implementations, or engineering efforts that involve multiple technologies or technical disciplines.
  • Engineering Lifecycle: Experience performing requirements analysis, solution design, alternatives analysis, integration, testing, implementation planning, documentation, and transition to operations.
  • Technical Mentoring: Experience providing technical guidance, peer review, training, or mentoring to other engineers. Formal supervisory or people-management experience is not required.
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Telecommunications, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related field.

Preferred Technical Proficiencies

  • VoIP and Telephony Protocols: Strong knowledge of SIP, SDP, RTP/RTCP, SRTP, H.323, MGCP, ISDN/PRI, and related signaling and media protocols.
  • Call-Control Platforms: Experience with enterprise platforms such as Cisco Unified Communications Manager, Cisco Unity Connection, Microsoft Teams Phone, or comparable on-premises and cloud-based call-control systems.
  • Dial Plans and Carrier Services: Experience with enterprise dial plans, E.164 numbering, digit manipulation, SIP trunks, PSTN connectivity, carrier interconnections, voice gateways, voicemail, and emergency calling.
  • VTC and Collaboration Systems: Experience designing, integrating, deploying, or supporting Cisco, Poly, Microsoft Teams Rooms, Zoom Rooms, Crestron, Webex, or comparable collaboration technologies.
  • Session Border Controllers: Experience configuring and troubleshooting AudioCodes Mediant, Ribbon SBC, Oracle Communications Session Border Controller/Acme Packet, Cisco CUBE, or comparable SBC platforms.
  • Cloud and Hybrid Voice: Experience integrating on-premises telephony with cloud collaboration services, including Microsoft Teams Direct Routing, Operator Connect, Webex Calling, or comparable platforms.
  • Network and QoS Analysis: Strong working knowledge of IP networking, routing, switching, VLANs, firewalls, Network Address Translation, SIP and media traversal, packet analysis, QoS policy design, and bandwidth planning.
  • Security and Identity: Working knowledge of SIP TLS, mutual TLS, SRTP, certificates and PKI, directory services, identity integration, secure configuration baselines, vulnerability remediation, and configuration management.
  • Troubleshooting Tools: Demonstrated ability to use Wireshark, platform traces, SBC logs, call-detail records, monitoring systems, and other diagnostic tools to isolate signaling, media, network, and interoperability problems.

Leadership and Communication Skills

  • Ability to independently lead complex technical efforts while collaborating effectively with project managers, engineering leaders, customers, and operations personnel.
  • Ability to provide technical direction and mentorship without relying on formal supervisory authority.
  • Strong judgment and decision-making skills, including the ability to evaluate alternatives and balance technical performance, cost, schedule, risk, security, and supportability.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts, risks, and recommendations to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
  • Ability to influence project and team leaders through sound engineering analysis, clear documentation, and well-supported recommendations.
  • Strong customer and stakeholder-management skills, including the ability to establish expectations, communicate constraints, and resolve technical disagreements.
  • Demonstrated problem-solving ability and experience working through complex or high-pressure engineering and operational situations.
  • Commitment to knowledge sharing, process improvement, engineering quality, and continuous technical development.

Preferred Certifications and Qualifications

  • Cisco Certified Network Professional Collaboration or a comparable voice, video, networking, or unified communications certification.
  • Cisco Certified Internetwork Expert Collaboration is beneficial but not required.
  • Current Microsoft certification related to Microsoft Teams Phone, collaboration communications systems, or an equivalent technology.
  • Current AudioCodes, Ribbon, Cisco, Microsoft, or comparable voice and collaboration certification.
  • Experience developing technical proposals, statements of work, bills of material, levels of effort, implementation plans, or technical risk assessments.
  • Experience with automation or scripting for telephony administration, data collection, validation, or provisioning using PowerShell, Python, REST APIs, or comparable technologies.
  • Experience supporting geographically distributed, highly available, or mission-critical voice and video environments.

NGEN

title: Engineering Technician III
description:
Job Description

Leidos Defense has an opening for an Engineering Technician III supporting our NATSC contract in Newport Rhode Island. The candidate, under the direction of the Engineering Manager and Production Support Supervisor, will support our Navy Array Technical Support Center (NATSC) contract at the Naval Undersea Warfare Center, Division Newport, Rhode Island. An Engineering Technician III performs assignments that are not completely standardized or prescribed, selects or adapts standard procedures or equipment, using fully applicable precedents, receives initial instructions, equipment requirements, and advice from supervisor or manager as needed, performs recurring work independently.

Primary responsibilities

A detail-oriented and highly capable Engineering Technician to join the Production Support team. In this role, you will be responsible for the repair, inspection, and preventative maintenance of Jigs, Tools, and Test Equipment (JTF). The ideal candidate is comfortable working independently on complex electrical and fiber optic assemblies, operating standard test equipment, and maintaining audit-ready documentation while mentoring junior staff. This role requires a balance of hands-on technical skill and the critical judgment needed to adapt standard procedures for non-routine troubleshooting and repair.

Specific Duties

  • Repair, modify, and troubleshooting modules or components.

  • Assemble or install equipment or parts that require simple wiring, soldering, or connecting.

  • Build and repair pigtail assemblies according to detailed documentation.

  • Build, inspect, polish, and test fiber optic cables.

  • Use test equipment to take measurements and readings to troubleshoot or repair JTF, equipment, or parts and components.

  • Conduct experiments and tests that may require minor test setup modifications and subjective judgment.

  • Perform PM’s on JTF, including fiber and electrical measurements. Apply necessary markings and safely work with hazardous materials as defined by established PM Cards.

  • Follow standard work methods on recurring assignments independently. Select and adapt standard procedures using fully applicable precedents.

  • Manage independent workstreams with minimal supervision while supporting broader team goals.

  • Receive explicit instructions for unfamiliar assignments.

  • Maintain a clean, safe, and organized work area at all times.

  • Provide regular status updates to the Supervisor.

Basic Qualifications

  • U.S. Citizenship required.

  • High school/vocational school diploma or GED certificate and 2+ years electronics repair relevant work experience or a related Technical School or Navy experience.

  • Experience using general purpose test equipment.

  • Candidates must be capable of soldering wires and inspecting and polishing fiber optic cables. The selected candidate will be provided with fiber optic and J-STD solder training.

  • Experience performing tasks using formal work procedures.

  • Ability to obtain and maintain a DOD secret level clearance. Must have a minimum of a DOD Interim secret level clearance to start in this position.

  • All employees must conduct themselves in accordance with Leidos Values and Business Ethics at all times.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Advanced degree from a Technical School a plus.

  • Knowledge of UTH operations or other production lines operations involved with position.

  • Knowledge of standard computer operations and Microsoft Office and programming software.

This position is covered under the Service Contract Act and is subject to minimum wage requirements as well as the minimum Health and Welfare benefit. Leidos will ensure that all provisions are met through their wages and benefits. The pay for this position will be $26.03/hr.

title: CSWO
description:
Leidos' Digital Modernization sector is seeking a Cyber Security Watch Officer (CSWO) to join the GSM-O effort at the Pentagon. This position will be supporting Day Shift.


Applicants must have a minimum Secret clearance with ability to obtain TS/SCI and must be available for shift work (including weekends), which may vary based on program needs and manning levels. We support 24/7 operations and while shift assignments are usually static, they are based on both preference and contract requirements, so we ask our team members to remain flexible to potential shift modifications to meet minimum staffing requirements. All new hires will spend a brief ramp-up period on weekday day shift to start.


Primary Responsibilities:

  • Support the Joint Network Operation and Support Center (JNOSC) Battle Captain and Cyber Center Security Chief with all cyber defense and network assurance issues.
  • Oversee all network defense operations, and be familiar with the operations process flow and execution.
  • Maintain awareness of all pertinent directives, orders, alerts, and messages; prepare and deliver daily situational awareness and operational update briefings.
  • Serve as Defensive Cybersecurity SME during 24x7 operations.

Required Clearance and Certifications:

  • Must have, at minimum, an active DoD Secret security clearance with ability to obtain TS/SCI (active TS/SCI preferred)
  • Must have DoD 8570 IAT II or higher certification (Security+ CE or equivalent) prior to start.


Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree and 3+ years of professional experience; additional military or relevant work experience may be considered lieu of a degree.

title: Lead Analyst, Publishing Analytics
description:
Why Sony Interactive Entertainment?

Sony Interactive Entertainment isn’t just the Best Place to Play — it’s also the Best Place to Work. Sony Interactive Entertainment (SIE) is the company behind the PlayStation brand. As a subsidiary of Sony Group Corporation, we’re part of a proud legacy of innovation and excellence. SIE is a dynamic technology company, delivering cutting-edge hardware and network services to more than 100 million people and an entertainment leader, home to some of the most beloved and recognizable intellectual properties (IP) in the world. Our role at SIE is to create and nurture the experiences under the PlayStation brand, a name synonymous with entertainment excellence and creativity.

About PlayStation Games and Publishing Analytics
In Games and Publishing Analytics, we partner with PlayStation Studios and global
publishing teams to help titles succeed across the full lifecycle. We bring together marketing,
audience, social, commercial, and product data to understand performance, evaluate
investment, and guide decisions from pre-launch planning through launch and live service.


We're looking for a Lead Analyst, Publishing Analytics who combines deep marketing-
measurement expertise with strong business judgment and a talent for turning fragmented
signals into clear, practical guidance. This role will lead high-impact programs across social
intelligence, marketing mix modeling, and publishing decision support while helping build
the data and analytical practices that allow the work to scale.


What you will be doing
As a Lead Analyst, Publishing Analytics, you'll work with Marketing, Community, Publishing,
Product, Analytics Engineering, Data & AI, and game teams to answer complex questions
about audience and player response, campaign effectiveness, marketing strategy, and long-
term title and franchise health.


You will:
• Lead social listening, sentiment, and creator analytics across PlayStation titles and
franchises, using sources such as Meltwater, Quid, community platforms, influencer
and streaming data, and first-party signals to identify shifts in conversation, content
performance, and emerging issues around campaigns, releases, and live-service
milestones.
• Develop, validate, interpret, and evolve marketing mix models that quantify the
contribution of paid, owned, and earned channels to revenue, demand, engagement,
and other business outcomes across live-service games.
• Own complex publishing analytics programs and stakeholder relationships for
multiple games across the portfolio, clarifying decision needs, setting the analytical
approach, managing milestones and risks, and driving work through adoption with a
high degree of autonomy.
• Create stakeholder-ready narratives and products that turn complex evidence into
concise presentations, dashboards, recommendations, and executive summaries
with clear implications and actions.
• Translate marketing measurement into practical investment guidance, using MMM,
incrementality, experimentation, and benchmarking to inform strategy, budget
allocation, channel planning, campaigns, and future tests.
• Deliver timely recurring and ad hoc decision support for live-service and brand-
marketing campaigns, events, content beats, launch windows, publishing
performance reviews, franchise programs, and critical business moments.
• Partner with Analytics Engineering and Data & AI teams to build scalable marketing-
data foundations and operationalize data pipelines.

What we are looking for
• Advanced applied analytics expertise demonstrated through high-impact work in
marketing, publishing, product, commercial, or customer analytics.
• Deep knowledge of marketing measurement, including marketing mix modeling,
incrementality, experimental design, attribution, causal reasoning, and budget-response
interpretation.
• Experience integrating and interpreting multi-channel marketing data across paid media,
owned channels, earned media, social and community, influencer and creator, sales,
finance, audience, and product-performance signals.
• Experience with social analytics, ideally using social-listening or influencer-measurement
tools and data such as Meltwater, Quid, YouTube, Twitch, Reddit, Steam, reviews,
forums, or comparable sources.
• Advanced SQL skills and strong proficiency in Python and/or R for joining complex
datasets, statistical modeling, reproducible analysis, validation, and automation.
• Strong consultative stakeholder leadership and autonomous program management
across Marketing, Publishing, Product Management, Finance, Production, Data,
Engineering, and game teams.
• Excellent data visualization and executive storytelling skills.

Domain Experience
• Experience in games, entertainment, digital media, subscription, or another rapidly
evolving live-service business.
• Familiarity with marketing effectiveness, audience development, launches, engagement,
monetization, and franchise health.

Bonus Points if You Have
• Experience mentoring analysts, raising analytical rigor, or applying responsible AI-
assisted workflows to improve quality and velocity.
• Experience with Looker, Power BI, MicroStrategy, Tableau, or another BI tool with a
semantic layer.
• Experience across live service or games with complex progression, economy, combat,
content, or social systems.

Your day at NTT DATA
The Associate Data Engineer is an entry level role within the Data Engineering job family. This role is, tasked with assisting with the transformation of data into a structured format that can be easily analyzed in a query or report.

This role is responsible for supporting with the development of structured data sets that can be reused or complimented by other data sets and reports.

This role analyzes the data sources and data structure and will design and develop data models to support the analytics requirements of the business which includes management / operational / predictive / data science capabilities.

title: Director Assortment Planning
description:
Your strategic leadership, analytical expertise, and passion for building customer-centric assortments make you a great fit for our Director, Assortment Planning position. Join our dynamic team today and find a rewarding career with a company that values you and all you bring to the table.


About Your Role:

As the Director, Assortment Planning at Dollar Tree, you will lead the strategy and planning capabilities that shape how we build assortments for our customers and drive profitable growth across the business. You will serve as a strategic partner and advisor to senior leaders across Merchandising, Inventory Management, Finance, and Operations, translating category strategies, customer insights, and financial objectives into actionable assortment plans.

Leading a team of 20+ Assortment Planning professionals, including Managers and individual contributors, you will build talent depth, elevate analytical rigor, and advance the tools, processes, and capabilities that enable better and faster assortment decisions. Your leadership will help optimize sales, margin, inventory productivity, and long-term growth while advancing Dollar Tree’s broader merchandising strategy.

Your day-to-day responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:

Strategic Planning & Business Leadership

  • Provide strategic leadership in the development and execution of assortment strategies that advance category financial objectives, customer value propositions, and Dollar Tree’s broader merchandising vision.
  • Drive innovation in assortment planning through thought leadership, best practices, and advanced analytical methodologies that improve decision quality, inventory productivity, and operational effectiveness.
  • Lead high-impact initiatives from concept through implementation, translating innovative ideas into scalable solutions that deliver measurable enterprise value.
  • Leverage customer behavior, internal insights, market intelligence, and external trends to identify opportunities and inform merchandising strategies and business decisions.
  • Simplify and optimize business processes by eliminating unnecessary complexity, streamlining decision pathways, and identifying opportunities for automation and improved ways of working.

Assortment Strategy & Planning

  • Lead the development and execution of customer-centric assortment strategies through Product Line Reviews, weekly decomposition processes, and disciplined financial oversight.
  • Partner with GMMs and Merchandising leaders to shape category strategies and tactics, translating customer insights, merchant vision, and business opportunities into actionable assortment decisions.
  • Provide strategic direction to the Assortment Planning team, ensuring high-quality plans that support merchant initiatives, end-to-end Product Line Reviews, business reviews, and key enterprise priorities.
  • Own the end-to-end assortment planning strategy, balancing customer needs, merchant vision, productivity, and financial objectives.
  • Drive assortments that optimize sales, margin, inventory productivity, and sustainable category growth.

Analytical Leadership & Innovation

  • Build and advance the analytical capabilities of the Assortment Planning organization, establishing a solution-oriented culture grounded in critical thinking, structured problem solving, and data-driven decision-making.
  • Equip the team to diagnose root causes, solve complex business challenges, and confidently leverage a robust ecosystem of data, tools, and planning methodologies.
  • Champion advanced analytics and AI-enabled capabilities, encouraging experimentation, innovation, and new ways of working that improve the speed and quality of assortment decisions.
  • Partner across Merchandising, Inventory Management, Finance, and other functions to translate analytical insights into strategies, decisions, and measurable business outcomes.
  • Advance planning capabilities across assortment planning, item planning, merchandise financial planning, store clustering, and related disciplines.

Team Leadership & Development

  • Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team of 20+ Assortment Planning professionals, including Managers and individual contributors.
  • Recruit and develop talent that combines merchant curiosity, analytical thinking, design thinking, and strong business acumen.
  • Create a culture of ownership and accountability by connecting individual work to customer and business outcomes and reinforcing accuracy, discipline, executional excellence, and independent critical thinking.
  • Establish training and development programs that strengthen technical, analytical, leadership, and business capabilities across the team.
  • Provide ongoing coaching and mentorship, helping associates achieve their professional goals while increasing their ownership of business outcomes.
  • Build a strong talent and leadership pipeline through clear career paths, cross-functional exposure, mentoring opportunities, and increasing levels of responsibility.
  • Foster a culture of continuous learning that keeps the organization current on emerging retail trends, planning methodologies, technology, analytics, and industry best practices.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Influence

  • Serve as a strategic partner and advisor to senior leaders across Merchandising, Inventory Management, Finance, Marketing, Sales, and Operations.
  • Facilitate cross-functional alignment around assortment priorities, inventory strategies, financial objectives, and key business initiatives within a complex matrixed environment.
  • Influence business decisions through strong analytical storytelling, clear recommendations, and an ability to translate complex information into actionable strategies.
  • Build strong partnerships across functions to ensure assortment strategies can be effectively executed throughout the organization.
  • Contribute to broader transformation initiatives and champion the adoption of new tools, processes, technologies, and capabilities.

What We’re Looking For:

  • 6+ years of progressive experience in retail planning, assortment planning, merchandise planning, inventory management, advanced analytics, or a related discipline.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Economics, Analytics, Finance, Merchandising, or a related field; Master’s degree preferred.
  • Deep understanding of retail planning principles, merchandising processes, and advanced analytics.
  • Demonstrated expertise in planning methodologies including assortment planning, item planning, merchandise financial planning, and store clustering.
  • Strong analytical and financial acumen with the ability to translate complex data into actionable business strategies.
  • Experience partnering closely with Merchandising and Inventory Management teams to drive measurable business results.
  • Demonstrated experience leading, developing, and building high-performing teams.
  • Strong strategic thinking, problem-solving, and change leadership capabilities.
  • Ability to influence senior leaders and drive alignment across multiple functions within a matrixed organization.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to effectively engage associates and leaders at all levels of the organization.
  • Ability to balance long-term strategic thinking with disciplined execution and operational excellence.

Salary Range: $185,000 - $203,500 base + bonus + equity
