title: Product Development Specialist
description:
Job Description:

Product Development Specialist

Collaborate with Innovative 3Mers Around the World

Choosing where to start and grow your career has a major impact on your professional and personal life, so it’s equally important you know that the company that you choose to work at, and its leaders, will support and guide you. With a wide variety of people, global locations, technologies and products, 3M is a place where you can collaborate with other curious, creative 3Mers.

This position provides an opportunity to transition from other private, public, government or military experience to a 3M career.

The Impact You’ll Make in this Role
As a Product Development Specialist, you will have the opportunity to tap into your curiosity and collaborate with some of the most innovative people around the world. Here, you will make an impact by:

  • Assuming technical leadership on NPI (New Product Introduction) and NTI (New Technology Introduction) initiatives
  • Developing and running simulations for Medium Voltage (MV) and High Voltage (HV) product designs.
  • Creating and CAD models and guiding design efforts across a broad range of applications and product portfolios in the electrical industry.
  • Supporting new products introductions in all stages of development from prototype development over feasibility demonstration to model validation and refinement.
  • Interfacing with cross-functional team members (marketing, manufacturing, supply chain, sales, technical service, quality, regulatory, etc) to ensure successful program delivery.
  • Generating intellectual property positions, including invention submissions, patents and 3M trade secrets. Leading technical interactions with corporate, group and division labs to identify new technologies, processes and materials to be applied to the Energy Markets
  • Developing and commercializing products to efficiently, reliably and sustainably deliver energy to customers around the world

Your Skills and Expertise

To set you up for success in this role from day one, 3M requires (at a minimum) the following qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher in engineering or science (completed and verified prior to start) from an accredited institution.
  • Three (3) years of product development, engineering or technical service in a private, public, government or military environment
  • Three (3) years of practical experience with CAD drawings and software

Additional qualifications that could help you succeed even further in this role include:

title: Taxonomist, Supply
description:
Brief info about Vinted

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life – or even a third.
The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people.

Information about the position

Vinted’s Supply domain drives the seller experience at Vinted, by developing easy listing experiences that produce high quality, searchable listings that sell fast. You’ll be working within the team, a cross-functional group of taxonomists, decision scientists, and product managers. Our goal is to enhance Vinted’s listing, browsing, search, and item retrieval. As a taxonomist, you will build the structural logic for navigation, search relevance, listing quality, and product expansion, ensuring a coherent, seamless, and relevant end-to-end category experience.These data models and structures help Vinted’s buyers find unique items and grow Vinted's global business. You’d be joining our team at a critical time: we are adapting our data models and systems to better support Vinted’s transformation into a multi-vertical marketplace.

As part of taxonomy projects, you will research, design, implement, and evaluate ontology and taxonomy changes. Your goal will be to promote and balance the needs of sellers and buyers in our C2C marketplace, as well as machine learning models. You will work closely with internal teams to explore alternative ways of modelling our data.

This role is perfect for someone who has experience designing and implementing taxonomies and ontologies, especially in an eCommerce environment.

In this position, you’ll

  • Design, revise, and maintain buyer and seller-facing product taxonomies and navigation, across a wide range of product verticals
  • Design, implement, and maintain ontologies and data structures that support our member-facing content
  • Balance Vinted’s Member experience with taxonomy and metadata heuristics while maintaining Vinted’s tone and voice.
  • Research and build product attributes to help buyers narrow their search, and sellers describe their items.
  • Work with user research and data analysts to build and test taxonomies and metadata structures for the most impactful results.
  • Document internal standards, workflows, governance processes, and data models.
  • Collaborate and connect with a wide range of internal teams including: engineers, product managers, designers, data scientists, legal, policy, communications, localisation, and customer support.

About you

  • Experience in developing taxonomies and/or ontologies to support a variety of systems both for front-end and back-end use.
  • Ability to clearly articulate the benefits of taxonomy and structured data to audiences of different knowledge levels and backgrounds.
  • Experience with evaluating and implementing taxonomies to support search systems, content management systems, metadata schemes, digital asset management systems, or product classification.
  • Experience building taxonomies for machine learning classification systems.
  • Strong logical thinker who loves finding practical solutions for users.
  • Fluency in taxonomy and ontology design principles, as well as information architecture.
  • Basic SQL and Excel/Google Sheets skills.
  • Experience with AI driven solutions
  • Strong communication skills, including excellent written and spoken English.
  • Bonus: Fluency in other Vinted market languages such as French, German, Spanish, Dutch or Italian.Bonus: Experience working in eCommerce environments
  • Bonus: Proficiency in ontology or knowledge graph development (e.g. RDF, OWL, and related tools)

Work perks

  • The opportunity to benefit from our share options programme
  • 30 days of paid annual leave
  • Newest MacBook models
  • Confidential Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for you and your family
  • Home office support: we provide IT workstation equipment and a personal budget of up to €540 for home workplace furniture
  • Lunch benefit per your workday
  • Frequent team-building events
  • A personal monthly budget for shopping on Vinted
  • Access to a discounted gym membership plan
  • Pension Plan with Vinted matching 150% of your chosen contribution
  • Supplemental Private Health Insurance
  • Life and Disability insurance
  • A subsidised Deutschlandticket for your commute to the office by public transport
  • A dog-friendly office

Working at Vinted

Workation policy

Better balance holidays with workdays by working remotely! Up to 90 days per year in the EU, of these, 21 days can be spent globally. For non-EU citizens, it's 21 days worldwide. This can be combined with time off for vacation or personal time.

Individual learning budget

Each year, you’ll be given a learning budget (starting at €3,000), and a total of up to 10 working days over a 2-year period to support your personal and professional development.

Hybrid work

Our hybrid model, with 2 recommended office days a week, gives you and your team the flexibility to decide if and when you want to work from home, and when to catch up in person.

Equal opportunity

We welcome applications from everybody, regardless of your background, identity, or life experiences. Job openings come with guides, not checklists. If you’re excited about a role, but don’t identify with every point in the ‘About you’ section, apply anyway – you might still be the perfect match!

€75.200—€101.800 EUR

Working at NLR

NLR is located at the foothills of the Rocky Mountains in Golden, Colorado is the nation's primary laboratory for energy systems research and development.

Join the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR), where world-class scientists, engineers, and experts are accelerating energy innovation through breakthrough research and systems integration. From our mission to our collaborative culture, NLR stands out in the research community for its commitment to an affordable and secure energy future. Spanning foundational science to applied systems engineering and analysis, we focus on solving complex challenges to deliver advanced, secure, reliable, and cost-effective energy solutions. Our work helps strengthen U.S. industries, support job creation, and promote national economic growth.

At NLR, you'll find a mission-driven environment supported by state-of-the-art facilities, multidisciplinary research teams, and strong collaborations with industry, academia, and other national laboratories. We offer robust professional development opportunities, and a competitive benefits package designed to support your career and well-being.



Job Description

National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) bridges research with real-world applications to advance new energy materials and technologies that lower costs, boost the economy, strengthen security, and deliver abundant and reliable energy. The Integrated Carbon Conversion Processes Group within NLR’s Catalytic Carbon Transformation and Scale-Up Center is seeking an Intern to provide researchers within our group the support necessary to achieve their cutting-edge research safely. . Our group’s mission is to de-risk and accelerate the scale-up of technologies for producing chemicals, fertilizers, and critical minerals from domestic biomass resources and waste resources. Our multidisciplinary team integrates expertise in process engineering, process science, catalysis, and computational modeling of integrated processes to translate laboratory discoveries into technically and economically viable processes suitable for pilot-scale demonstration and eventual commercialization. The directorate’s research encompasses multiple areas including analysis & characterization, biochemical processes, downstream processing, bioenergetics, and thermochemical processes.

Our research group is focused on developing chemicals, critical minerals, fertilizers, and materials from terrestrial and algal biomass. Our team brings together a wide range of technical expertise and global experience unified by a passionate drive to increase the technoeconomic feasibility and global adoption of biorefineries. Interdisciplinary collaboration and a relentless pursuit of advancing understanding at the intersection of fundamental science and industrial application is paramount to every member of our team.

The successful candidate will perform hands-on tasks and experimentation in a laboratory setting including the following:

  • Batch and flow reactor operation for algal pretreatment, conversion, chemical production and polymer synthesis
  • Develop renewable polyurethane materials for a broad range of applications.
  • Benchtop wet chemistry, including sample preparation and derivatization,
  • Operation and maintenance of analytical instrumentation, (e.g. FTIR, NMR, TGA, DSC, GC-MS, etc.)
  • Separations, including liquid-liquid and solid-liquid extractions.
  • Bioprocessing scale-up

The ability to conduct laboratory experiments and follow written procedures, with minimal supervision and with the utmost regard to safety is required. Self-motivation, adaptability and an aptitude for learning are critical for this role.

This is an excellent opportunity for a student invested in the NLR mission who desires relevant laboratory experience in preparation for graduate school or a career in the chemical industries.

Degree in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Biological Systems Engineering, Polymer Chemistry, or related discipline.

.

The Sponsor’s unit provides data management support for a large, high-visibility area of responsibility.

The Sponsor requires support in all aspects of the data management lifecycle, with a focus on advancing data management tasks, tracking data lifecycle processes, and implementation of the Sponsor’s rules and regulations.

The work may be performed independently or within a team environment.

The Sponsor needs skills in metadata and data management; cataloging; data ingestion; data sharing; and strong interpersonal skills to be able to work with other units as required.

The Sponsor project manager will manage the priorities.

The Data Analyst will identify and catalog datasets relevant to the AOR and track datasets through their lifecycle; catalog datasets and records of varying volume, content, and structure following Sponsor requirements, standard operations procedures, and best practices, and provide ad hoc reports from the data catalog on specific topics requested by Sponsor.

They will monitor data submissions and track through ingestion lifecycle; monitor data submissions and track through data ingestion lifecycle; coordinate with the Sponsor and system teams to troubleshoot data management and ingestion issues; and provide support and advice to the Sponsor for data submissions.

The Data Analyst will also support the creation of workflows, visuals, and briefing materials for presentations as requested by the Sponsor; participate in regular meetings under the direction of the Sponsor; coordinate with the Sponsor to adjust data management priorities as needed; and provide support to the Sponsor’s organization for data sharing with other organizations.

They will support the Sponsor’s data compliance objectives by monitoring, tracking, and updating email groups and the training status of stakeholders and coordinate with the Sponsor to ensure all data handling decisions are tracked in enterprise data catalog.

  • Must have a TS/SCI with Poly

title: Hospital Based Bilingual Patient Advocate (rotating weekend coverage 1x per month)
description:
Make a real difference in patients’ lives—join Elevate Patient Financial Solutions as a Hospital Based Bilingual Patient Advocate and help guide individuals through their healthcare financial journey. This full-time position is located 100% onsite at a hospital in Falls Church, VA, with a Monday-Friday schedule from 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM with rotating weekends (1 per month).
Bring your passion for helping others and grow with a company that values your impact. In 2024, our Advocates helped over 823,000 patients secure the Medicaid coverage they needed. Elevate’s mission is to make a difference. Are you ready to be the difference?
As a Hospital Based Bilingual Patient Advocate, you play a vital role in guiding uninsured hospital patients through the complex landscape of medical and disability assistance. This onsite, hospital-based role places you at the heart of patient financial advocacy—meeting individuals face-to-face, right in their hospital rooms, to guide them through the process of identifying eligibility and applying for financial assistance. Your presence and empathy make a real difference during some of life’s most vulnerable moments.
Job Summary
The purpose of this position is to connect uninsured hospital patients to programs that will cover their medical expenses. As a Patient Advocate, you will play a critical role in assisting uninsured hospital patients by evaluating their eligibility for various federal, state, and county medical or disability assistance programs through bed-side visits and in-person interactions. Your primary objective will be to guide patients face-to-face through the application process, ensuring thorough completion and follow-up. This role is crucial in ensuring that uninsured patients are promptly identified and assisted, with the goal of meeting our benchmark that 98% of patients are screened at bedside. This position is responsible for working as the liaison between the patient in need, the hospital facility and government agencies, proficiently and effectively communicating in English and Spanish.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
  • Screen uninsured hospital patients at bedside in an effort to determine if patient is a viable candidate for federal, state, and/or county medical or disability assistance.
  • Complete the appropriate applications and following through until approved.
  • Detailed, accurate and timely documentation in both MPower and the hospital systems on all cases worked.
  • Provide exceptional customer service at all times.
  • Participate in ongoing trainings in order to apply the content learned in dealings with patients and cases.
  • Maintain assigned work queue of patient accounts.
  • Collaborate in person and through verbal/written correspondence with hospital staff, case managers, social workers, financial counselors.
  • Answer incoming telephone calls, make out-bound calls, and track (via MPower) all paperwork necessary to submit enrollment and renewal for prospective Medicaid patients.
  • Maintain structured and timely contact with the applicant and responsible government agency, by phone whenever possible or as structured via the daily work queue.
  • Assist the applicant with gathering any additional reports or records, meeting appointment dates and times and arrange transportation if warranted.
  • Request home visits as needed to acquire documentation.
  • As per established protocols, inform the client in a timely manner of all approvals and denials of coverage.
  • Attend ongoing required training to remain informed about current rules and regulations related to governmental programs, and apply updated knowledge when working with patients and cases.
  • Regular and timely attendance.
  • All other duties as assigned
Qualifications and Requirements
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or abilities.
  • High School Diploma or GED preferred, except when required by our client.
  • Prior hospital experience preferred
  • Adaptability when dealing with constantly changing processes, computer systems and government programs
  • Professional experience working with state and federal programs
  • Critical thinking skills
  • Ability to maneuver throughout the hospital and patients’ rooms throughout scheduled work shift.
  • Proficient experience utilizing Microsoft Office Suite with emphasis on Excel and Outlook
  • Effectively communicate both orally and written, to a variety of individuals utilizing fluent Spanish and English.
  • Ability to multitask to meet performance metrics while functioning in a fast-paced environment.
  • Hospital-Based Patient Advocates are expected to dress in accordance with their respective Client’s Dress Code.
  • Ability to multitask
  • Ability to function in a fast-paced environment

This role operates within a SAFe/Agile framework as part of an Agile Release Train (ART) delivering iterative value across the program.


In this position, you will serve as the Product Owner for a development team in an Agile/SAFe environment, owning the team backlog and assisting in the design and implementation of software solutions alongside your team while working with program architects, customer stakeholders, Product Management, and DevSecOps teams. You will translate platform and mission capability needs into testable, prioritized work that the team can deliver predictably in a highly regulated, safety-critical environment.


This is a hybrid position requiring 3 days onsite and 2 days working from home, if you are located within a commutable distance (Less than 1 hour's drive one-way during normal traffic) from Gaithersburg, MD; Eagan, MN; or Egg Harbor Township, NJ. However, if you do not reside within a commutable distance, you may be considered for a 100% remote role.


This role focuses on building and modernizing real-time, safety-critical systems using a combination of traditional systems engineering and AI-augmented software development practices. You’ll work on software that directly supports national air traffic operations, applying AI tools to accelerate development, improve quality, and enhance system reliability.


Primary Responsibilities

  • Own and prioritize the backlog for one or more Agile teams, sequencing work based on stakeholder needs, program priorities, and dependencies, and ensuring the development team builds the right functionality
  • Review program requirement documents, system specifications, and applicable FAA standards and orders to extract intent, constraints, and acceptance criteria
  • Decompose high-level platform and mission capability needs into specific, testable capability statements (Agile features and stories) with clear acceptance criteria
  • Maintain traceability from source requirements through features, stories, and verification evidence, ensuring compliance outcomes are demonstrable
  • Engage customer stakeholders to identify use cases with an emphasis on completeness, testability, alignment with operational workflows, and readiness for validation and field activities
  • Define team PI objectives, participate in PI planning and backlog refinement, make timely scope decisions, and accept completed work
  • Systematically capture and communicate design decisions, performance trade-offs, compliance rationales, and risk assessments with each release, enabling reviewers to trace decision-making and provide informed feedback
  • Prepare and review technical documentation, including use cases, user interface specifications, and interface definitions
  • Coordinate with the Release Train Engineer, Product Management, systems engineering, and Test and Evaluation to manage dependencies and align delivery with integration and verification milestones
  • Lead and participate in structured reviews and inspections

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related discipline with 8+ years of relevant experience, or a Master's degree with 6+ years of relevant experience. (Equivalent experience may be used in lieu of degree)
  • Experience and familiarity with Agile methodology, principles, and tools
  • Experience in the role of Agile Product Owner, including owning and prioritizing the product backlog, defining complete product backlog items (user stories), making timely decisions on scope, and acceptance of work
  • Demonstrated ability to decompose complex requirements into testable work items with clear, verifiable acceptance criteria
  • Strong understanding of disciplined engineering processes, including attention to detail
  • Past practical exposure to writing, testing, debugging, and maintaining software or scripts
  • Experience with the design of cloud-based systems
  • Experience in engaging customers to understand needs, deliver solutions, manage expectations, and maintain an ongoing relationship
  • Experience working within a Scaled Agile (SAFe) organization, including PI planning and cross-team coordination
  • Clear and effective verbal and written communication
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust
  • U.S. citizenship required
  • Successful completion of background investigations as required by the government customer

Preferred Qualifications

  • Knowledge of and experience with AI-assisted development workflows and tools (Claude Code, Codex, etc.)
  • Experience with Java, Python, React, and scripting languages
  • SAFe Product Owner / Product Manager (POPM) certification
  • Knowledge of and experience with DevSecOps practices and CI/CD pipelines
  • Knowledge of hybrid cloud data mesh architectures and microservices platforms
  • Familiarity with MBSE concepts and systems engineering integration
  • Knowledge of air traffic control systems, air traffic management, general aviation, and/or flight services
  • Practical knowledge of FAA/DoD systems, technical policies, standards, and orders
  • Knowledge of FedRAMP, FISMA, or government security compliance frameworks
  • Experience supporting verification and validation of safety-critical systems
  • Track record of successful delivery on large government programs
  • Desired but not required: Commutable distance to Gaithersburg, MD; Eagan, MN; or Egg Harbor Township, NJ.

Why Leidos?

You’ll work on systems where performance, precision, and reliability matter — every second. This is not experimental AI for prototypes. This is disciplined, responsible AI applied to mission-critical software that supports national infrastructure.

If you’re excited by solving complex problems in regulated, real-world environments — and using AI as a force multiplier rather than a shortcut — we’d like to talk.

title: Maintenance Tech Assistant
description:
Ferco Tech is seeking a motivated Maintenance Technician Assistant to support the maintenance of our manufacturing facility, production equipment, and building systems. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who has basic maintenance or mechanical knowledge and is interested in developing their skills in an industrial manufacturing environment.

The Maintenance Technician Assistant will work closely with and receive hands-on training and mentorship from our experienced Maintenance Technician. The ideal candidate does not need to know everything on day one—we are looking for someone who is mechanically inclined, dependable, safety-conscious, willing to learn, and comfortable working with hand tools and performing basic facility maintenance.

As skills and experience develop, this position will be given increasing responsibility for preventive maintenance, equipment troubleshooting, repairs, and facility maintenance.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

The ideal candidate will be able and willing to:

  • Assist the Maintenance Technician with routine maintenance and repair of production machinery, equipment, and plant facilities.
  • Perform basic facility maintenance, including minor plumbing, carpentry, painting, hardware replacement, and general building repairs.
  • Assist with scheduled preventive maintenance on production machines, equipment, and facility systems.
  • Learn to identify and troubleshoot basic mechanical, electrical, pneumatic, and hydraulic issues under the guidance of the Maintenance Technician.
  • Assist with diagnosing equipment problems, replacing components, testing repairs, and making basic adjustments.
  • Learn to read and understand equipment manuals, work orders, schematics, and maintenance instructions.
  • Safely use hand tools, power tools, ladders, material-handling equipment, and other maintenance equipment.
  • Assist with emergency or unscheduled equipment repairs as needed.
  • Learn and follow proper Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures before performing maintenance or repairs.
  • Inspect equipment and facility areas for potential maintenance or safety concerns and report issues to the Maintenance Technician or appropriate supervisor.
  • Assist with maintaining maintenance tools, supplies, parts, and work areas in a clean and organized condition.
  • Support facility and environmental activities, inspections, and projects as needed.
  • Participate in company safety initiatives and follow all established safety procedures.
  • Maintain clean and orderly work areas.
  • Work cooperatively with production employees, supervisors, and other departments to support facility and equipment needs.
  • Perform other maintenance, facility, or operational duties as assigned by the Maintenance Technician, Plant Manager, or other members of the leadership team.
  • Perform all responsibilities in a safe and appropriate manner while maintaining acceptable levels of quality and efficiency.

Experience and Education

  • High school diploma or GED required.
  • Basic knowledge of general building, facility, mechanical, or equipment maintenance preferred.
  • Previous experience performing basic repairs, working with tools, automotive repair, construction, manufacturing, facilities maintenance, or a related field is preferred but not required.
  • Previous manufacturing experience is a plus.
  • Mechanical aptitude and an interest in learning industrial maintenance are strongly preferred.
  • Trade school, vocational training, or coursework in industrial maintenance, mechanical systems, electrical systems, HVAC, or a related field is a plus but not required.
  • Basic understanding of electrical, mechanical, pneumatic, hydraulic, plumbing, or carpentry systems is a plus.
  • Must be willing and able to learn new maintenance skills through hands-on training and mentorship.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Mechanically inclined with basic troubleshooting skills.
  • Comfortable working with common hand and power tools.
  • Willingness and ability to learn from an experienced Maintenance Technician.
  • Strong attention to safety and detail.
  • Dependable and able to follow through on assigned tasks.
  • Self-motivated and able to work independently once properly trained.
  • Ability to follow verbal and written instructions.
  • Good communication and teamwork skills.
  • Ability to recognize when an issue requires assistance from a more experienced Maintenance Technician or outside service provider.
  • Willingness to take on increasing responsibility as knowledge and skills develop.

Position Demands

  • Ability to lift and/or move up to 75 pounds.
  • Ability to stand and walk for extended periods throughout the workday.
  • Ability to bend, twist, turn, carry, sit, stoop, kneel, crouch, and climb as required.
  • Ability to safely work from ladders or at heights when properly trained and using required fall-protection equipment.
  • Ability to safely work around manufacturing machinery and equipment.
  • Ability to work safely with hazardous chemicals and wear required personal protective equipment.
  • Extended hours or overtime may occasionally be required during peak workloads, equipment issues, or special projects.

Schedule

Monday – Thursday: 6:00 a.m. – 4:30 p.m.
Overtime: Fridays as needed

Export Control Requirements

This role is restricted to U.S. persons (i.e., U.S. citizens, permanent residents, and other protected individuals under the Immigration and Naturalization Act, 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3)) due to access to export-controlled technology. Proof of applicable status will be required prior to employment.

Benefits

Ferco Tech offers a competitive benefits package, including:

  • Medical and other benefit options
  • 401(k) with company matching
  • Paid time off
  • Paid holidays
  • Hands-on training and development
  • Opportunity to develop industrial maintenance skills and grow within the organization

title: Chief Personal Property Appraiser - Jefferson County (Tax Assessor - Birmingham)
description:
TARGET CLOSE DATE:

10/02/2026

PAY GRADE:

Grade 28

TYPE:

Full time

JOB SUMMARY:

The Jefferson County Commission Tax Assessor’s Birmingham Office is seeking a motivated and experienced Chief Personal Property Appraiser to lead the operations of the Personal Property Section. The incumbent will plan, direct, and coordinate the work of staff to ensure personal property is accurately assessed and properly classified in accordance with applicable laws, policies, and procedures.

The Chief Personal Property Appraiser will oversee a department or division, coordinate staff activities, and review the work of subordinates for technical accuracy and compliance with governing requirements. This position requires extensive knowledge of laws, regulations, and ordinances related to the appraisal and assessment of personal property, as well as strong leadership and organizational skills.

Work is primarily performed in an office setting with minimal physical demands. Some travel may be required to conduct field reviews.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS:

Jefferson County provides competitive pay and comprehensive benefits packages to include medical and dental insurance, employer-sponsored retirement plan (pension), generous paid holidays, sick and vacation leave, and more. The pay range for this job is presented below:

$74,068 - $114,899

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

The following are job-related qualifications that are required for employment consideration for this position:

  • Possession of a State Certified Appraisal Certificate (i.e., from any state).

  • Coursework in basic principles of accounting.

  • Experience creating spreadsheets to perform calculations.

  • Experience performing audits.

  • Experience appraising equipment, furniture, and fixtures.

  • Experience in disputes of valuation (e.g., protests, appeals, litigation).

TARGETED QUALIFICATIONS:

The following are job-related qualifications deemed desirable by Jefferson County. These qualifications may be considered when reviewing applications and inviting candidates to participate in subsequent steps in the selection processes.

  • Experience with Alabama Tax Code Title 40 (Revenue and Taxation)

TYPICAL JOB DUTIES:

  • Performs administrative duties (e.g., writing reports, maintaining files, drafting mail correspondence, communicating information, providing assistance) in order to maintain efficient departmental operations.

  • Assists taxpayers with various issues related to personal property (e.g., completing forms, answering questions, resolving complaints)..

  • Oversees and/or conducts business inspections in order to identify taxable personal property items and assess appropriate tax amounts for revenue purposes.

  • Develops and/or participates in the development, interpretation and/or implementation of goals, objectives, policies, procedures, and/or laws in order to provide direction, vision, and operational standards for the department.

  • Gathers evidence and reviews documentation (e.g., income and expense statements, private appraisals, deeds, liens, mortgages, market trends, attorney general opinions, case law, blueprints, sketches and drawings, legal descriptions) in order to obtain relevant information related to citizen protests of assessed property values and/or related court cases.

  • Engages in activities designed to ensure professional development, awareness of developments in the field, and knowledge of relevant practices, rules, laws, policies, and/or guidelines.

  • Makes decisions and renders judgments based on property-related evidence/information in response to citizen protests of assessed property values and/or related court cases.

  • Supervises staff by assigning and distributing work, directing staff in their job duties, monitoring progress of work, providing feedback and/or training

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

Job is primarily sedentary involving sitting for long periods of time, but may involve occasional walking or standing for brief periods. May involve occasional light lifting of items or objects weighing up to 25 lbs.

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

Work is conducted both indoors in an office setting as well as regular field visits to external places of business, residence, or construction worksites. Work involves use of standard office equipment, such as computer, phone, copier, etc.

title: Senior Windows SME
description:
Leidos is committed to delivering innovative solutions and supporting mission-critical operations for our customers. The DISA CESO ITSS team provides network operations and cyber defense support to the Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA), enabling secure and reliable communications for the Department of Defense (DoD) and Combatant Commands (COCOMs).

Leidos is seeking a Senior Windows Systems Administrator (SA) to serve as the primary Windows SA and subject matter expert (SME) for our team. This role focuses on ownership of our Windows environment while supporting a mixed‑OS infrastructure.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Serve as the senior lead and primary Subject Matter Expert (SME) for all Windows Server environments, driving technical strategy, architecture decisions, and operational excellence.

  • Design, architect, implement, and sustain enterprise Windows infrastructure.

  • Own the health, performance, and availability of Windows systems; proactively monitor, analyze trends, and implement improvements to prevent issues before they impact operations.

  • Lead complex troubleshooting and incident resolution efforts, conducting deep root cause analysis and implementing permanent corrective actions across systems and services.

  • Establish and enforce enterprise standards, baselines, and hardening guidelines in alignment with security frameworks and compliance requirements.

  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to system administrators and engineers; guide best practices and elevate team capabilities across Windows technologies.

  • Lead planning and execution of system lifecycle activities, including patching, upgrades, migrations, and modernization initiatives.

  • Provide cross-platform support by performing basic Linux system administration and coordinating with Linux SMEs for complex issues.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in a related discipline with 8+ years of prior relevant experience, or master’s degree with 6–10 years of prior relevant experience.

  • Security+ Certification or other DOD 8570 IAT Level II Certification

  • Security Clearance Requirement: Active TS and SCI eligibility

  • Strong experience administering Windows Server environments.

  • Deep understanding of core Windows services and system management.

  • Working knowledge of Linux systems.

  • Solid troubleshooting and communication skills.

title: Head of Information Management
description:
The Head of Information Management will lead the evolution and execution of the organisation’s enterprise-wide information management strategy, ensuring that data and information assets are governed, structured, and secured in line with regulatory, legislative, and nuclear industry standards.

Working closely with the CISO and other key stakeholders, the role will build on and develop the information management programme that underpins secure, compliant, and value-driven information practices across the business. This includes the evolution of arrangements with core partners and customers, enshrining compliance and commercial objectives; the maintenance of process and policy suites to provide ongoing, relevant structure to shape wider data and digital activities and initiatives across the organisation; as well as the development of a structured assurance programme to embed new and existing practices while providing active confidence to key stakeholders of the organisation’s progress in information maturity.


The role is responsible for:-

Accountable on behalf of the CDIO on overseeing the company direction on information by working with multiple business areas to ensure information is managed and owned by the business and can be used for value in the organisation. The role holder will work with the CISO,delivery Heads and other key business stakeholders in defining, owning and delivering the strategy on information

Strategic Leadership

· Define and lead the enterprise-wide information management vision, strategy, aligned with cyber security, compliance, and business objectives

· Oversee and manage the information and data process for the organisation

· Drive a programme of change/training that embeds secure information practices throughout the organisation’s culture, technology, and operations

· Manage and own the development of the company IMS data/information related processes

· Champion the value of information as a corporate asset and support digital transformation programmes with strong data governance principles.

· Oversee and support the management of information between the company and its core parter and customer organisation.

· Maintain a holistic view of all information-related activity and initiatives in the organisation.

· Provide conflict resolution and a mechanism for pragmatic decision making in key digital areas.

Policy and Governance

· Develop, implement, and maintain information and data policies, standards, and procedures aligned with regulatory (e.g. GDPR, NIS2), legal, and nuclear sector-specific obligations in alignment with architectural and data teams.

· Lead business-wide Information Management Group to ensure cross-functional alignment and oversight.

· Ensure data classification, labelling, and handling policies are up to date and operationally effective.

· Manage information risk management for the CDIO.

Compliance and Industry Alignment

Ensure compliance with applicable standards, such as:

· ONR Security Assessment Principles (SyAPs)

· ISO/IEC 27001 and 27701

· IAEA nuclear information guidance

· Data Protection Act 2018 / UK GDPR / EU AI Act

· Collaborate with Legal, IT, and Compliance to manage data-related regulatory risks

· Support audits and regulatory inspections relating to information management and cyber security

· Act as sponsor for information related non-conformance / compliance remediation.

Programme Delivery

· Lead and evolve the multi-year information management programme, including risk assessment, remediation, controls implementation and how we exchange data with our partners/customers/suppliers/shareholders

· Define and track KPIs for information management maturity and assurance

· Manage vendor relationships and solution implementation related to document management, data discovery, and classification tools

Stakeholder Engagement & Change Management

· Work with business unit leaders, IT, and project managers to ensure that information principles are embedded into new projects and systems

· Lead training and awareness campaigns related to information governance, policy, and compliance.

· Act as the senior point of contact for all enterprise-wide information management concerns


What we're looking for

  • Ability to demonstrate tangible examples of setting a strategy, governing and managing Information Management frameworks, policies and procedures. Able to establish programmes of work to deliver the strategy
  • ​​Able to partner with business and drive outcomes​
  • Can provide clear experience in managing business relationships, get teams to deliver when not in direct control of the resource
  • Can demonstrate creation of strategies and plans for Information Management
  • Excellent communicator at all levels and using multiple methods. Able to rationalise complex
  • information (both high level and detailed level) to make it understandable for others to work with.
  • Conveys information and ideas clearly, accurately, and persuasively.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills to proactively eliminate problems and ease the path to delivery of delightful user experiences
  • Degree level or equivalent
  • Recognised and related qualifications/training in Information Management/privacy/security

Location & Ways of Working

This role can be based in Derby, Manchester or Warrington, with flexibility to work between home and the office depending on business needs. There may be some international travel required on an ad hoc basis.


Reward & Benefits

  • Salary Range: £85,600 - £114,400
  • Bonus: Up to 20% plus 15% long term incentive cash plan
  • Benefits allowance: £8,500
  • Pension: Standard Rolls-Royce SMR pension 12%
  • Holiday: 28 days plus bank holidays
  • Flexible and inclusive working environment

Selection Process

Shortlisted candidates will be invited to a competency‑based interview and may be asked to provide evidence of document management capability. This role requires BPSS checks as part of our onboarding process.


Inclusion & Accessibility

We’re committed to building a diverse, inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued. If you meet around 75% of the criteria, we’d still love to hear from you. We’re happy to discuss reasonable adjustments throughout the recruitment process and offer flexible or part‑time working where possible.

Why Join Us?


You’ll be joining a forward-thinking organisation that values transparency, fairness, and innovation. We offer:


• A flexible, inclusive, and supportive working environment.
• Opportunities for career growth in a rapidly scaling business.
• A culture that values diversity, innovation, and continuous learning.


We are an equal opportunities employer and welcome applications from all backgrounds. Inclusivity is important to us, and as a Disability Confident organisation, we are committed to fair, supportive, and continually improving recruitment practices that ensure everyone has the opportunity to thrive.


Confidence can sometimes hold us back from applying for a job. But we'll let you in on a secret: there's no such thing as a 'perfect' candidate. If you feel you meet 75% of the requirements for this role, we would love to hear from you.


Also, if you are considering a career move or a sector-jump, please get in touch – we welcome applications from people with transferable skills.

Our Application Process

title: Senior Client Project / Programme Manager
description:

Your day at NTT DATA
The Senior Client Project / Program Manager is an advanced subject matter expert, responsible for leading and directing concurrent client projects classified as standard or complex.

This role may also be involved in larger-scale programs and is responsible for delivery across multiple business areas, geographies and technologies.

The primary responsibility of the Senior Client Project / Program Manager is to interface with all project stakeholders to take projects from original concept through to final implementation, including handing over to Operations (whether internal to organization or to the client's support operations).

This role may take responsibility for the management of projects and programs within more complex/partnership accounts and collaborate and engage with senior members involved in program delivery at the client site.

In this instance, the Senior Client Project / Program Manager leads the coordinated management of multiple related projects within a program to achieve the business objectives and ensure the strategic benefits are transitioned to the client organization.

Key responsibilities:

title: Program Manager (NASA JSC)
description:
Leidos has a contingent opening for a Program Manager (PM) supporting the Exploration, Environment & Earth Intelligence Division within Leidos. This position will execute and implement strategy, support services and overall contractor activities and deliverables for NASA contracts. The PM serves as the primary point of contact for the customer and provides technical supervision, and manages contractor personnel assigned to the program. The PM is responsible for assessing the market for new and innovative projects and professional services, and in partnership with business development, supports activities for on-contract growth and new business opportunities. The ideal candidate will live near NASA JSC.

Primary Responsibilities:

  • Serving as the single point of accountability for overall contract performance, managing scope, cost, schedule, staffing, and technical quality.

  • Primary point of contact for the Contracting Officer (CO), Contracting Officer's Representative (COR), and customer technical leadership.

  • Building strong relationships with customers ensuring complete customer satisfaction

  • Planning, organizing and managing multiple teams led by managers and/or supervisors to meet contact requirements across multiple technical scope areas:

    • Supporting systems engineering & integration, and analyses for simulation and spaceflight software
    • Developing and maintaining simulation models, applications and products (including virtual reality products) for training and engineering analysis.
    • Maintaining and verifying spaceflight software (including software lab management)
    • Developing and testing models and hardware for guidance, navigation, communication and advanced robotics, and supporting advanced spaceflight software R&D
    • Assessing software requirements/designs/certification/etc. for space vehicle system management, and developing human-rated safety-critical and non-safety critical spaceflight software

  • Working with task and functional leaders, other companies and support personnel, defining approach and schedules with assigned personnel, and establishing budgets for contract labor resources, equipment, and supplies.

  • Oversight of contract management tasks to meet quality, safety, OCI, property management, and information/IT security obligations defined per contract provisions.

  • Ensuring that the program organizational structure is optimal and staffed with the appropriate levels of skills across multiple disciplines within a contract.

  • Managing external relationships with other companies and clients.

  • Communicating program status to customer per contact requirements and to Leidos Management.

  • Support proposal, recompete, and business-growth activities, including identification of adjacent mission work and positioning for follow-on task orders.

title: Senior Associate, Online Safety Supervision
description:
Closing Date:

28/09/2026

Group:

Online Safety Group

Management Level:

Senior Associate

Job Type:

Fixed Term (Fixed Term)

Job Description:


Please note that this role will close at 00:01 on Monday 28 September, and therefore we advise getting your application in by no later than midnight on Sunday 27 September.


How to Apply


Please submit your CV and a covering letter of no more than a page in length answering the following question:


Tell us about a time in which you managed a project from beginning to end in which managing internal and external stakeholders was key to success.


Your CV and cover letter should be uploaded as one document at the point where you are asked for your CV. Applications without the covering letter will be deemed as incomplete. If you need any support, please reach out to Laura.King@ofcom.org.uk.


We have two fixed-term positions available, we expect them to last for 12 months.


About the Team


The Online Safety Group’s purpose is to ensure UK citizens have a safer life online by implementing and overseeing the requirements under the Online Safety Act 2023. The Group is responsible for delivering online safety policy, supervising online services, and building technical expertise to meet the regime's aims.


This role sits within Ofcom’s Supervision Team. The Supervision Team provides close, structured engagement with specific services in scope of the online safety regime, alongside an approach to promoting compliance across many thousands of services. This role will consider industry practices in good governance and standards in online safety risk assessments, working closely with other specialist teams in Ofcom and the supervision team to identify improvements.



Purpose of the Role


Our Supervision Senior Associates manage our engagement with some of the online services people use every day. You will directly supervise key tech firms, building healthy relationships so we can understand their user protections and, where necessary, encourage them to do better. As you grow into the role, we’ll support you in building your knowledge of online safety measures and the services you supervise, so you can become an expert in protecting users from harmful and illegal content.


You will be working as part of a team to supervise a portfolio of key services. You will develop supervision strategies for each service and report on progress against them to the wider Online Safety Group. You will be Ofcom's main point of contact for your services, ensuring that all of Ofcom’s engagement and requests for information align with its strategic aims while balancing proportionality.


Senior Supervision Associates also play a role in compliance delivery programmes across key harm areas, which align with Ofcom’s strategic priorities. This activity involves driving programme management across several services.


Content information and safeguarding


Applicants should be aware that whilst these roles should not involve direct exposure to illegal content, they could include working time spent on distressing content, material, and themes. Ofcom is committed to safeguarding our colleagues who undertake this type of work and offers a range of tailored support options, including training, annual psychological assessments for those regularly doing this work and 24-hour access to counselling services.


Your key responsibilities


  • Build and maintain strong relationships with relevant online services
  • Develop deep expertise in your supervised services and across Ofcom’s online safety programme, keeping across online safety, markets and tech developments
  • Understand, assess and, where necessary, drive improvements in protections offered to users and other obligations under the Online Safety Act
  • Identify and drive research, information gathering and analysis about the services you supervise and ensure analysis and outputs are drawn together for the wider team
  • Ensure the delivery of clear, concise and focused documents, such as briefings and research reports, for internal use or external publication
  • Oversee and manage the workload of junior and cross-functional colleagues as needed to ensure we deliver against our strategic priorities
  • Build and maintain effective relationships with teams across Ofcom that work with us, ensuring they are updated, included and feel heard
  • Deliver or contribute to initiatives across the Supervision Team to support our strategy, e.g. international or cross-regulatory engagement or developing expertise in specific markets
  • Ensure clear communication and information sharing at all levels with the rest of the Online Safety Group and deliver clear updates on the services you supervise when requested.
  • Drive effective programme management of compliance delivery for a strategic priority, including developing OKRs, effective prioritisation of issues, and supporting and working with relevant supervision teams to help them meet deadlines.

The skills, knowledge and experience you will need for success


  • Articulating Ideas: Presentation and drafting skills, with the ability to produce clear, concise and understandable communications or documents for internal and external use.
  • Experience of working in complex policy compliance or with regulatory issues
  • Scanning Horizons: Grasp the bigger picture, foresee upcoming trends and challenges, and ensure actions and decisions are in sync with long-term objectives.
  • Executing Plans: Organise tasks and set clear goals, managing resources wisely while monitoring progress.
  • Embracing Change: Remain flexible in the face of change, anticipating and adjusting to shifts.
  • Harmonising Work: Work effectively with others, creating an honest team environment and sharing valuable information and resources.
  • Channelling Influence: Guide opinions and decisions with compelling communication and persuasion techniques, aiming to get everyone on the same page.
  • Empowering Development: Support others in growing their skills and strengths. Empower them with guidance and let their potential shine.

Inclusive hiring at Ofcom


At Ofcom, our mission is clear: to make communications work for everyone. To achieve that, our people must reflect the diversity of the UK, in background, identity and experience.


We believe innovation thrives when difference is valued and everyone feels empowered to contribute their ideas and perspectives. That’s why we welcome colleagues of all ethnicities and races, sexes, genders and gender identities, sexual orientations, ages, faiths and beliefs, and those with apparent and non‑apparent disabilities. We value socio‑economic diversity, life experience and neurodiversity too. Whether you’re a carer, a parent, a veteran, or re‑entering work after time away, your voice and perspective matter here.


Flexibility is at the heart of how we work because we want you to thrive in a way that suits you best. Most roles can therefore be adapted for part‑time hours, job shares, or other flexible arrangements. Learn more about our Rewards, Benefits and Wellbeing on our careers page.


Our recruitment process is intentionally designed to be open and accessible. If you need adjustments, information in a different format or an alternative way to apply, contact us at resourcing@ofcom.org.uk or 0330 912 1378.


As a proud Disability Confident Leader, we guarantee interviews for disabled applicants who meet the essential criteria for a role. You can read more about this commitment here.


Whoever you are, whatever your story, you belong at Ofcom.

title: Technical Test Services Evaluation Manager, AI Tester Accreditation Programme (AI TAP)
location: IMD - Mapletree Business City, MBC BLK 10
description:
[What the role is]

About Us
AI Verify Foundation is an open-source initiative and a wholly owned subsidiary under the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA), dedicated to advancing trustworthy AI. We develop and maintain open-source tools for evaluating LLM applications (Project Moonshot) and predictive ML models (AI Verify Toolkit). Our mission is to empower developers, data scientists, and organisations to build responsible, transparent, and reliable AI systems.

The AI Verify Foundation's AI Tester Accreditation Programme (AI TAP) is the first programme of its kind in Asia, accrediting testing service firms that can technically assess AI systems for safety, reliability, and governance risks. Accredited firms are recognised by AI Verify Foundation as having possessed the technical competencies and operational readiness to evaluate AI systems against a defined scope to provide AI system developers, deployers, and end users with greater confidence in independently assessed AI.

You will be part of a dynamic team driving the growth of Singapore's AI assurance ecosystem. In this role, you will lead the end-to-end accreditation process for AI testing service providers, evaluate their technical and operational capabilities, and work closely with industry stakeholders to shape emerging standards for AI technical testing. You will also engage with businesses seeking qualified AI assurance testers, connecting them with accredited firms and supporting the broader development of a trusted AI assurance marketplace.

You will collaborate with local and international industry partners, government agencies, and internal teams to continuously refine the programme's assessment scope and standards, ensuring AI TAP remains credible, rigorous, and relevant in a rapidly evolving AI landscape.

[What you will be working on]

  • Lead and manage the full accreditation lifecycle for AI testing service providers, including application review, technical evaluation, accreditation decisions, and annual renewals.
  • Evaluate applicant firms against defined accreditation criteria, covering technical testing competency.
  • Assess firms' claimed AI testing services against established guidelines and frameworks (e.g., IMDA Starter Kit for Testing LLM-Based Applications for Safety and Reliability).
  • Engage with industry stakeholders, testing service providers, and AI system developers and deployers to understand evolving needs and refine the programme's assessment scope and standards.
  • Develop and maintain accreditation documentation, evaluation rubrics, and assessment guidelines to ensure consistency and rigour across all accreditation reviews.
  • Monitor developments in AI testing methodologies, safety frameworks, and governance standards to ensure the programme remains current and credible.

[What we are looking for]

(A) Academic

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field.
  • Professional certifications in AI governance (e.g., AIGP: Artificial Intelligence Governance Professional) or GenAI / Agentic AI testing are advantageous.

(B) Experience

  • Minimum of 3-5 years of experience in GenAI / Agentic AI systems evaluation, technical testing, software quality assurance, or a related field.
  • Strong working knowledge of AI system development lifecycles, including Generative AI and LLM-based applications, and associated safety and reliability considerations.
  • Demonstrated experience in designing or managing accreditation, certification, or audit programmes is highly desirable.
  • Familiarity with AI governance frameworks, responsible AI principles, and technical testing standards (e.g., IMDA AI testing guidelines, ISO/IEC AI standards).
  • Experience engaging with senior stakeholders across industry, government, and technical communities.

(C) Other Key Areas of Consideration

  • Strong analytical and evaluative skills, with the ability to assess complex technical claims and make well-reasoned accreditation judgements.
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with both technical experts and non-technical stakeholders (including C-suite executives and policy makers).
  • Self-motivated and adaptable, with the ability to operate effectively in a nascent and evolving programme environment where standards and processes are still being shaped.
  • Commercially aware, with an understanding of the AI testing services market and the business considerations of testing service providers.
  • Plugged into the AI, tech, and assurance ecosystem in Singapore, with a genuine interest in advancing the responsible development and deployment of AI.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to produce clear, well-structured evaluation reports and programme documentation.

Position will be commensurate with the candidate’s qualifications and experience.

Please note that only shortlisted candidates will be notified.

description:
Director, Workplace Services & Operations (Interim). Nairobi. Posting Date: 09/18/2026. Deadline: 10/09/2026

Role Title: Director, Workplace Services & Operations (Interim)

Contract Type: Fixed-Term, 12–18 months

Workstyle Arrangement: Hybrid

Reporting To: Chief Operating Officer

Department: Office of the COO

Location: Nairobi, Mexico City, Bogota, Rio de Janeiro

Team Name: Global Operations and Real Estate

Role Purpose

The Interim Director, Workplace Services & Operations provides executive leadership for the organization's global workplace services portfolio, encompassing real estate, facilities management, office operations, and associated operational support services. Reporting to the COO, the role is accountable for maintaining safe, reliable, inclusive, and cost-effective services across a geographically distributed office footprint while leading in partnership with the COO, a time-bound evolution and alignment of functions priorities.

Over the 12–18-month assignment, the Director will stabilize service delivery, surface synergies and integrate currently separate capabilities, clarify ownership and decision rights, and establish consistent governance, service standards, performance measures and commercial disciplines. The role will assess the current operating model and deliver an evidence-based future-state model that improves accountability, customer experience, operational resilience, value for money, and scalability.

The Director will lead managers and teams through change, partner with senior leaders and local offices across jurisdictions, and provide the COO and executive leadership with clear insight into risks, performance, priorities and investment decisions. Success requires a seasoned and credible global workplace leader who combines strategic judgement with hands-on operational stewardship, organizational design, transformation delivery, commercial acumen and inclusive people leadership.

Key responsibilities

Strategic and operational leadership

  • Set the direction and priorities for global Workplace Services & Operations, translating organizational priorities into a clear portfolio plan.
  • Maintain continuity, safety, resilience and service quality across real estate, facilities and office operations, intervening decisively where performance or risk is outside tolerance.
  • Advise the COO and executive leadership on workplace strategy, portfolio risks, investment choices, performance and emerging operational issues.

Service integration and operating-model transformation

  • Lead a comprehensive current-state review of services, structures, accountability, capacity, demand, costs, contracts, systems and ways of working.
  • Integrate currently separate workplace capabilities and develop a service catalogue that defines customers, service owners, standards, escalation routes and service levels.
  • Design and implement an approved future-state operating model, including organization structure, role clarity, governance, decision rights, capabilities and resource requirements.
  • Simplify processes, remove duplication, and embed continuous improvement disciplines across the portfolio.

Governance, performance and commercial stewardship

  • Establish new (and/or improve existing) portfolio governance, risk controls, management information, KPIs and SLAs, and provide regular executive reporting with clear recommendations.
  • Own portfolio budgets, forecasts and resource allocation, ensuring responsible expenditure, value for money and alignment with organizational priorities.
  • Oversee strategic vendors, contracts and procurement activity; strengthen supplier performance, commercial terms, compliance and risk management.
  • Ensure global policies and operating standards are practical, consistently applied, and appropriately adapted to local legal and operational requirements.

Stakeholder and change leadership

  • Build trusted relationships with local offices, functional leaders and senior stakeholders to understand needs, manage trade-offs, and improve the workplace experience.
  • Lead consultation, communication and change activity in a transparent, inclusive and culturally sensitive manner that sustains engagement and service continuity.
  • Represent the portfolio in enterprise forums and model the organization's values internally and externally.

People leadership

  • Lead, coach and hold managers accountable for delivery, collaboration, workforce planning, and the development of their teams.
  • Assess capability and succession needs, create development opportunities and foster an equitable, inclusive, service-oriented and high-performing culture.

Key assignment deliverables

  • A validated current-state assessment covering services, demand, structure, capability, costs, contracts, performance, risks and stakeholder experience.
  • An agreed service catalogue, accountability framework, information flow and portfolio governance model.
  • A prioritized operational improvement plan with measurable efficiency, service quality, and risk reduction outcomes.
  • A sustainable performance dashboard and executive reporting cadence.
  • A handover plan at the end of the assignment.

People Responsibilities (Total Team/DRs)

Yes (2 direct reports and 28 FTE in total)

Service continuity and critical incident performance; stakeholder satisfaction; achievement of portfolio KPIs and SLAs; budget and forecast performance; vendor and contract performance; risk and compliance; process efficiency; implementation of the approved operating model; and team engagement and capability.

Key Internal Relationships

COO; Managing Directors for Operations (People & Culture, IT, Finance, OGC, Grants Management and Global Safety & Security); Opportunity Directors; Managing Directors for Programs, Justice Initiative and Impact Investment.

The ideal candidate

  • Substantial senior leadership experience across workplace services, corporate real estate, facilities management or office operations in a complex, geographically distributed organisation.
  • Proven accountability for a multi-country service portfolio, including service continuity, operational risk, customer experience and local regulatory considerations.
  • Demonstrated success leading organizational transformation, operating-model design, service integration and implementation in an ambiguous environment.
  • Experience leading people managers and sizeable multidisciplinary teams, with evidence of improving accountability, capability, engagement and performance.
  • Strong budget ownership, forecasting and resource-allocation experience, together with oversight of significant supplier contracts, procurement and commercial negotiations.

title: Military Family Life Counselor (Child Development Center)
description:
Leidos is hiring licensed behavioral health professionals to join our Child and Youth Behavioral, Military and Family Life Counselor (MFLC) team to support Naval Base San Diego, CA.

Join the mission to support U.S. military service members and their families as they work through important military life adjustments while serving their country. The Child and Youth Behavioral Military and Family Life Counselor (CYB-MFLC) position offers a unique opportunity to serve a vital role, in providing non-medical support, which includes counseling, consultation, and outreach, to eligible faculty, staff, parents, children, and youth. Non-medical counseling is preventive in nature and aims to address and provide solution focused approaches to issues before they become greater challenges.

Military children face unique emotional and environmental challenges due to the stress of military life. This is an opportunity for you to reach them where and when you are most needed.

CYB-MFLC responsibilities include:

  • Work at installation Child Development Centers (CDCs) with children 0-5, before or after-school care centers for school-aged children, youth and teens on educational activities and appropriate developmental focus.
  • Observe, participate, and engage in activities with children and youth; provide coaching, guidance and support to staff and parents; and model behavior management techniques for staff and parents.
  • Offer presentations to address social skills development and social emotional learning that is crucial for childhood early development.
  • Promote creativity and positivity through approved materials.
  • Build rapport with parents and families by attending installation and community events.
  • Help children with transition adjustments, such as a new school and a new home.
  • Participate in regular in-service training or other contract activities as assigned.
  • Communicate information regarding trends and issues at assigned installation to Team Leads.

CYB-MFLC will also benefit from:

  • No insurance to file.
  • No progress notes required.
  • No treatment plans to develop.
  • iPad provided for easy digital reporting, with no PII or PHI.
  • Paid federal holidays.
  • Free and unlimited behavioral healthcare training.
  • Reimbursement for job-related license renewal fees.
  • Eligibility to participate in 401K retirement plan.
  • Centralized support through a Counseling Center of Excellence that provides best practices, expert speakers, and state-of-the-art resources.

Additional Job Duties May Include:

  • Responding to emergent situations in any physical location on a military installation
  • Traversing long distances to both indoor and outdoor locations, to maneuver through rugged, outdoor, or uneven locations (ascend/descend), and work in outdoor weather.
  • Travelling to locations outside of a military base in a variety of physical environments.
  • Due to the nature of working on military installations or related worksites, counselors may need to comply with various site-specific requirements to work at designated locations.

Environment:

At the direction of the Department of Defense, duties are performed in multiple indoor locations (approximately 60%) and outdoor locations (approximately 40%). The indoor locations are located within a child development center (CDC) controlled by the Department of Defense. The outdoor locations frequently involve traversing over uneven grassy, gravel, and/or dirt areas, ascending/descending stairs, and exposure to the weather. CDC settings frequently involve sitting on the floor to interact with children for up to 2 hours at a time.

Licensure Portability:

Great news! In accordance with the recent National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), licensed Military and Family Life Counselors may provide non-medical counseling services to military families at any location in a U.S. state, the District of Columbia, or a territory or possession of the United States, regardless of which state the counselor is licensed in. Within the scope of the MFLC program, a counselor may hold any independent and clinical license recognized by the Secretary of Defense as an appropriate license for the provision of non-medical counseling services.

Minimum Requirements:

  • A master’s degree or higher in the Behavioral Health Professions (MS/MSW/MA/PhD).
  • Licensure to practice at the independent practice level (LCSW, MFT, LPCC, Psychologist) in the United States.
  • Must be a U.S. citizen.
  • Must be able to pass a basic background check for employment, a Child National Agency Check, and Inquiries (NACI/CNACI) clearance, commonly called a Public Trust clearance.

title: Business Analyst
description:
About Leidos Australia


At Leidos Australia, our work goes beyond a job title. We design, build, operate and support the systems, services and capabilities that help protect and advance the Australian way of life.


Backed by a global organisation of more than 40,000 people, our Australian team of around 2,000 has partnered with government, defence and national security customers for more than 30 years. We deliver mission-critical solutions where reliability, trust and purpose matter.


Leidos is a destination for people who want their work to have purpose, their contribution to be recognised, and their career to grow without needing to fit a single mould. Meaningful work is supported by benefits, flexibility and career pathways that help you grow while balancing life outside work. This includes:


  • Flex Your Way – Tailor work to your life with options including Life Days (up to 12 extra days off per year), part-time arrangements, job sharing, and compressed hours.
  • Wellbeing That Matters – Free access to Headspace and MeQuilibrium, plus dedicated wellness spaces to support your mental, physical, and emotional wellbeing.

About the Team


You’ll join a team where people work with integrity, inclusion, innovation, agility, collaboration and commitment. In practice, that means sharing ownership, solving complex problems together and staying connected to the customer context, the purpose behind the work and how each role contributes to meaningful outcomes.


Mission Software Systems (MSS) brings together expertise across intelligence, software, and cloud to deliver end-to-end capability supporting the full intelligence lifecycle, from planning through to dissemination and feedback. The team fosters a culture of innovation, leveraging modern engineering practices and shared infrastructure to rapidly build, test, and deploy software solutions across a range of environments, including cloud. MSS also plays a key role in advancing technology modernisation within Government, delivering scalable and adaptable solutions for complex enterprise challenges.


The Opportunity


As a Senior Business Analyst, you will play a pivotal role in shaping and delivering technology solutions that address complex business challenges and create meaningful outcomes for customers and stakeholders. Working across cross-functional teams, you will bridge the gap between business needs and technical delivery, ensuring solutions are practical, scalable, and aligned to strategic objectives.


In this role, you will:

  • Partner with business stakeholders, product owners, solution architects, developers, and delivery teams to elicit, analyse, and document complex business and system requirements.
  • Lead discovery, process mapping, impact assessments, and solution design activities to support the delivery of enterprise software applications, integrations, and digital transformation initiatives.
  • Translate business needs into clear user stories, functional and non-functional requirements, process models, and acceptance criteria, enabling delivery teams to build high-quality solutions.
  • Drive stakeholder engagement throughout the project lifecycle, supporting prioritisation, solution validation, testing, change implementation, and continuous improvement within an Agile delivery environment.

About You


You are an experienced Business Analyst who enjoys working at the intersection of business and technology. You bring a consultative approach, are comfortable navigating ambiguity, and have a proven ability to turn complex requirements into practical software solutions. You thrive in collaborative environments and can confidently engage with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Experience working with Agile delivery methodologies and practices, including user story development, backlog refinement, and sprint-based delivery.
